## 2026-11-10 — Session 228: a line is an accountability, not a readership — per-line 1:1 body confidentiality (Schema v132 unchanged, [ADR-0165](docs/adr/0165-per-line-one-on-one-confidentiality.md), `#/oneonones` + person page + prep sheet)

**Why this item / coverage.** Selected from Planned because frontline / mid-manager × matrix was the least recently primary altitude (Session 221) and this was the named merge blocker of the Session 227 1:1 draft now on `main`: `scopedViewState` passed any meeting naming a line-reached person into the projection **in full**, so a second-line manager read the home manager's private 1:1 — notes, mood, agenda, promises — on the same screens the home manager used. Session 226 had reproduced it on a live fixture and named it; this session closed it. **Altitude: frontline / mid-manager PRIMARY** (rank ≤2 is where conversation detail lives); **structure: matrix** — single-chain and the undeclared operator view are pinned byte-identical by test.

**Built.** One rule, one place, no second hierarchy (`app/core/domain/meetingPrivacy.js`, on the same `buildMatrix` → `buildSeats` engine): the recorded holder reads their own room; a **different recorded holder** identifies the room and nobody outside it reads inside it — not the home tree, not a peer, not an ancestor at rank ≤2; an **unattributed** (legacy) row keeps the pre-ADR-0165 tree visibility — exactly the world a single-chain workspace lives in — while an additional-line seat is shown the FACT (id, person, date, `dateUncertain`, status, holder triple) with every conversational field emptied and the reason printed, never a silent blank. Stubbing happens only in the per-render `scopedViewState` projection; disk bytes are never touched; persisted schema is unchanged (Schema v132). The three legacy write doors (`toggleMeetingAction`, `addMeetingAction`, `setActionOwner`) now refuse a meeting that is not the seat's room (`meetingBodyRefusal`, fail-closed on an unresolvable boundary); `logOneOnOne`'s cross-line rules already refused closing another line's promise and are unchanged. The 1:1 view, person page and prep sheet print the printed reason instead of content; quality grades and promise counts are computed only from conversations the seat may read; a withheld meeting renders date/status/holder plus a lock line. ADR-0086 consented release grants remain the one legitimate cross-boundary path for content; claiming an unattributed meeting is recorded attestation (reversible, audited), never a door into a room that names a different holder.

**Built in this branch.** Schema v132 adds a holder, attribution basis and timestamp without guessing historical holders. Held 1:1s logged under a rank-1/2 seat use that seat; an operator may choose a holder or leave it unknown. The read model treats uncertain dates and active structural defects cautiously; scoped aggregates are withheld in higher-altitude or mixed-detail cases. Director/VP line holders cannot log through the current rank-1/2 right. Coverage uses today's lines and may credit a meeting predating a line; ended/re-established line history is not reconstructed. Previously repaired invalid dates cannot be recovered, and the legacy person-level cadence can still use fallback dates. Seats are workflow declarations, not authentication.

## 2026-11-10 — Session 226: matrix 1:1 line coverage — pure read model committed, NOT wired; nothing user-visible shipped

**Discovery before selection.** Four leadership-tool gaps were found by inspection and added to Planned below: (i) social-choice aggregation of competing line priorities; (ii) Leader Standard Work and tiered daily management; (iii) resource levelling of dated cross-line demands; (iv) per-line confidentiality of 1:1 records in a matrix. Evidence: `grep -rliE` over `app/` returns 0 files for `condorcet|borda|kemeny|schulze`, for `gemba|standard work|tiered daily`, and for `heijunka|load-level|resource level`; (iv) was observed on a live fixture (a manager who reaches a person only through an additional line reads the home manager's 1:1 with that person in full).

**Why this item / coverage.** Frontline / mid-manager × matrix was the least recently primary altitude (Session 221). The defect, reproduced on untouched `main` (an engineer with a home manager and a 40% project line): a stored 1:1 records who it was *with* and never who *held* it, so `cadence()` reads "the latest meeting with this person". One meeting by the home manager turns the person green for every seat while the project line has never met them, and the reverse. The second line cannot record its own meeting at all: under the project manager's seat `logOneOnOne` is refused with `scope-refusal`. Duty targeted: every manager who holds a line on a person owes that person a standing conversation, and a silent line must be visible rather than masked by a busy one.

**Built — foundation only, imported by nothing in the running app.** `app/core/domain/oneOnOneLineRegistry.js` (vocabulary, defaults, method and limits text, CSV columns), `oneOnOneLineSchema.js` (normalizers for a per-meeting holder — an unaccountable one is cleared and counted — for the conventions and for a marker ledger, plus a validator that refuses an out-of-range convention instead of clamping it) and `oneOnOneLines.js`, a pure read model: one reading per (person, line) pair — on cadence, due, overdue, never held, new, cannot be read, exempt — with home-line thresholds identical to `cadence()`; *masked* when the people list reads on track while a line is silent; a meeting with no holder makes a line *unreadable* only where it could change the reading, and never credits or condemns one; pair states and meeting classes each reconcile to their totals; disclosure follows the existing 1:1 record policy (named, counted only, or withheld); the brief and the CSV rows carry no identity. Plus `tests/app/one-on-one-lines.test.mjs`. `LeadOS-standalone.html` is re-stamped only: the modules are outside its import graph, so the bundle is byte-identical.

**Explicitly In Progress — remainder, which is everything a leader would use.** No holder is stored: `schema.js` is untouched (still v131), `logOneOnOne` stamps nothing, and the project line is still refused at the gateway. On real data every meeting therefore reads "no holder recorded" and no masked line can be proven — the suite pins that boundary. Not built: the three meeting fields and their migration, seat-derived stamping, the gateway line scope, the claim / release / conventions / scan commands and their governing right, `RULE-OOL-01` dated asks on the automation spine, the `#/matrix?panel=one-on-ones` panel and the held-by field in the 1:1 dialog, the CSV scope, and ADR-0164. Those names are reserved, not shipped; goal carriage also pencils in Schema v132, so whichever lands first takes it.

## 2026-11-10 — Sharing people requires an explicit operating interface, not silence or guessed escalation: Matrix Management-Interface Operating-Agreement Register (Session 223, Schema v131, [ADR-0162](./docs/adr/0162-matrix-management-interface-operating-agreements.md), `RULE-MIA-01`, CSV #122, `#/matrix?panel=interfaces`)

**Implemented — director / VP PRIMARY × matrix; CEO / C-suite read the aggregate portfolio board and apex roll-ups; frontline / mid-manager act as first-person counterpart managers; single-chain supported and inert.** The real duty: ADR-0161 (Session 222) exposed which counterpart managers share multi-line people and how scattered each span is, yet two managers sharing Sam still had no dated, bilateral, auditable record answering *how do we consult on priority and capacity trade-offs, which forum settles disputes, who sits at the joint apex above us, and when does this agreement expire?* This delivers the exact Planned item discovered in Session 222.

**Built.** Additive Schema v131 (`matrixInterfaceAgreements`, bounded `matrixInterfaceMarkers`, clamped `matrixInterface*` conventions, `MIGRATIONS[130]`), leaf registry (`matrixInterfaceRegistry.js`), fail-closed schema normalizers (`matrixInterfaceSchema.js`), pure read model (`matrixInterface.js`), governed command handlers (`matrixInterfaceActions.js`), shared-spine post-commit rule (`RULE-MIA-01` in `matrixInterfaceRules.js`, bringing the shared spine to **102 rules / 102 contracts**), aggregate-only CSV scope #122 (`matrix-interfaces`, **121** total registered scopes), and interactive panel (`matrixInterfacePanel.js` mounted at `#/matrix?panel=interfaces`).

**The refusals are the product.** (1) **Seven closed interface states with strict precedence**: `structurally-unresolvable` → `contested-terms` → `forum-unavailable` → `expired` → `one-sided` → `unagreed` (including future-dated bilateral terms counted in `futureDatedN`) → `current`. (2) **First-person bilateral standing & anti-forgery guard**: neither counterpart manager nor a peer seat may sign for the other side (`actingSide`/`actingManagerId` forgery is explicitly refused); bilateral status requires matching terms (`consultationRule`, `forumId`, `escalationSeatId`, `effectiveFrom`, `reviewByOn`) from both sides; retirement preserves history append-only. (3) **Live DAG apex & re-org invalidation**: escalation owners are checked dynamically against `matrixJointApex`; incomparable minimal ancestors (diamond ties) or disconnected managers mark `structurally-unresolvable` and refuse binding; a subsequent reporting-line change that moves the unique apex above a previously signed escalation owner shifts an agreed pair to `structurally-unresolvable`. (4) **No auto-renewal & no partial/small-cell coverage %**: expired agreements move to `expired`; retiring a named `cadenceForums` forum shifts the pair to `forum-unavailable`; workspace `coveragePct` is withheld when active line defects exist (`invalidLineN > 0`) or fewer than the small-cell floor (`3` pairs) are in scope. (5) **Scoped secrecy & aggregate-only export**: `RECORD_POLICIES` sets `detailCeiling: 0` on raw ledgers; rank `>= 4` scoped seats redact peer names/prose while preserving counts; CSV #122 and `matrixInterfaceBriefText` emit aggregate pair counts and apex buckets only with zero person, manager, forum, or basis text. (6) **`RULE-MIA-01` zero-churn episode asks**: fires on matrix line, forum lifecycle, interface lifecycle, and `matrix.interface.scan` events; inert in single-chain on automatic commits; issues at most 12 dated review delegations per commit to the unique `matrixJointApex` with `issues-obligation` + `rolls-up-to` edges, preserves a single active ask across uncovered negotiation states (`unagreed` → `one-sided` → `contested-terms`), closes automatically once `current`, and refuses to guess on diamond ties or disconnected pairs.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **director / VP primary 223** (with CEO / C-suite portfolio board & frontline manager first-person counterparty standing); frontline / mid-manager 221; CEO / C-suite 220. **Structure: single-chain 1–188; MATRIX primary 189–198, 200, 203, 204, 206, 208–223.** Single-chain unchanged: no pair, no agreement ask, and `RULE-MIA-01` inert on automatic commits. Next rotation: **CEO / C-suite × matrix** (last primary 220), starting with the Session 223 discovery (Matrix goal & key-result line-attribution and attainment double-counting audit).

**Verified.** `node --test tests/app/matrix-interface.test.mjs` (**6/6 PASS**); focused matrix/CSV/schema/authority/accountability verification across updated and adjacent suites (**100% PASS** after aligning 16 `SCHEMA_VERSION` `131` pins, `csv.test.mjs` `121`, and 4 adjacent `CSV_EXPORTS.length` pins `118 → 121`); `npm run verify:standalone` (**7/7 PASS**, `LeadOS-standalone.html` rebuilt at schema v131); `#/matrix?panel=interfaces` axe-core audit clean (`0` violations, `0` console errors); `npm run lint`, `npm run check:boundary`, and `npm run check:links` **PASS**.

## 2026-11-10 — A line charged 40% of a person that did nothing all quarter: Matrix Line Activity Reconciliation (Session 221, Schema v130 unchanged, [ADR-0160](./docs/adr/0160-matrix-line-activity.md), CSV #120, `#/matrix?panel=activity`)

**Implemented — frontline / mid-manager PRIMARY × matrix; director / VP / CEO read the same figures as a roll-up; single-chain supported and inert.** The real duty: ADR-0158 (Session 219) prices what each declared line was CHARGED across a period. Nothing said what each line DID. So two structures the matrix creates were invisible: a line declared at 40% of a person that originated **no dated act about her at all** for a whole quarter — nobody briefed her, no manager answered for the share, no term was re-affirmed, not one obligation the line left behind was settled — and a line declared at 10% that originated more of her line-addressed acts than every other line together. On paper she is 40% theirs; nobody is running it. That is the finding a frontline lead needs at week six, not a quarter-end story about a person.

**A structural fact found while building it, and what it changed.** Session 219's Planned item compared declared share-days to **completed work items**. Inspecting the record showed that this cannot be done honestly: an item names the PERSON, not the line it served, so a person on three lines makes every item she touches reach all three (`matrixWorkReach` reports exactly that, `sites.length > 1`). Attributing one item to one line would be an allocation this product invented. What the record DOES say exactly is which manager originated each dated act, about which person, on which day — four collections that had never been read together (`onboardingLineBriefs` ADR-0150, `lineConsents` ADR-0148, `lineReaffirmations` ADR-0157, `lineExitRemedies` ADR-0152). The observed side is those acts, and it is exact rather than inferred. The allocation-to-output item therefore stays Planned, recorded below as **blocked on line attribution on work records** — a prerequisite that must be built before that comparison can exist at all.

**Built.** One bounded pure read model (`lineActivity.js` + `lineActivityRegistry.js`), one panel (`matrixActivityPanel.js`, `#/matrix?panel=activity`) and one aggregate CSV scope (#120, `line-activity`) — **NO schema move, NO collection, NO stored field, NO rule, NO action**: everything printed is derived on read. The declared side is ADR-0158's ledger reused verbatim (one pricing engine, not two); the observed side is every dated act whose OWN day falls inside the SAME named window. Both sides are converted to whole per-mille by exact largest-remainder allocation, so each sums to exactly 1000 and the identity is printed as a claim (`sharesReconcile`, separate from `countsReconcile`). Five placement classes and eight verdicts with declared precedence (`refused` → `insufficient` → `unattributable-dominant` → `silent-line` → `over-active` → `under-active` → `sole-line` → `aligned`), a per-line-holder roll-up with a rate only above the declared floor, the identity-free brief, and a method block that names the reading's limits.

**The refusals are the product.** (1) **An act from a manager holding TWO of the person's priced lines is never assigned to one** — the record does not say which declaration it belonged to, so it is `ambiguous` and counted, and a person dominated by ambiguous acts reads `unattributable-dominant` rather than publishing a comparable minority as the whole. (2) **An act from a manager whose declared line the period could not price refuses the person's whole comparison** — the observed side is complete and the declared side is not, so no share is compared (`refused`, reason printed); the act is never dropped to make the arithmetic close. (3) **Acts from the home manager are counted and never charged to a line**: ADR-0158 prices additional lines only and the home pointer moves (ADR-0149), so a home act is `home`, printed, and out of scope on both sides. (4) **Below the declared floor of 3 attributed acts no share is compared** — the count is printed instead. (5) **A sole priced line is `sole-line`**, because it necessarily receives everything attributed and there is no second share to compare. (6) **Nothing is retuned, no manager is scored and no person is rated**: every verdict is about a LINE, and the panel, the brief and the export each say that the observed side counts dated acts — not hours and not work items — so the gap is a screening signal about which lines are being run, never a measurement of managerial effort or quality.

Next rotation: **director / VP × matrix** (last primary 219, the oldest).

## 2026-11-10 — Closing a drifted portfolio without rewriting history: Frozen Authority Re-Affirmation & Drift Settlement (Session 220, Schema v130, [ADR-0159](./docs/adr/0159-frozen-authority-reaffirmation.md), `RULE-ACR-01`, CSV #117 extended, `#/matrix?panel=continuity`)

**Implemented — CEO / C-suite PRIMARY × matrix; director / VP settle contested or multi-principal drift as joint matrix principals; frontline / mid-manager stand behind or refer drifted records on lines whose live right they hold; single-chain supported and inert on automatic commits.** The real duty: ADR-0156 (Session 217) gave the C-suite and board pack a portfolio read over frozen decisions (`merit-cycle`, `decision`, `board-memo`), comparing each record's frozen authority against the structure on its own effective date — and deliberately left every `drifted` verdict permanent forever. Once an organisation reorganised under a sound prior pricing decision, arbitration, or merit pool, `#/matrix?panel=continuity` refused the portfolio claim forever, even after the current authority holder reviewed the file and confirmed it still stands, leaving no auditable distinction between unreviewed structural drift and human-reconciled continuity (ISA 560 subsequent-event governance; Korn/Ferstl 2013 re-attestation). This was the exact Planned item Session 217 discovered for the CEO / C-suite × matrix rotation.

**Built.** Append-only settlement storage in Schema v130 (`authorityReaffirmations` + bounded `authorityReaffirmationMarkers`, `authorityReaffirmationSchema.js`, `MIGRATIONS[129]` migrating to empty arrays with zero fabricated attestations), live-matrix authority resolution and standing guards in `authorityContinuity.js` (`resolveCurrentAuthority`, `canSettleAuthority`, `allRows` pre-seat scope invariant), two governed actions (`authorityReaffirmStandBehind`, `authorityReaffirmRefer` in `authorityReaffirmationActions.js`) plus explicit `authorityContinuityScan`, one post-commit propagation rule (`RULE-ACR-01` in `authorityContinuityRules.js`, bringing the shared spine to **100 rules / 100 contracts**), additive columns on CSV scope #117 (`authority-continuity`), and interactive settlement controls on `#/matrix?panel=continuity` (`matrixContinuityPanel.js`).

**The refusals are the product.** (1) **History is never rewritten**: a settled record keeps `verdict === 'drifted'` and `populationClaim` remains `false`; `reconciledClaim` is computed and printed beside `populationClaim` and is granted only when covered population meets the declared floor (`>= 3`), zero `unattributed` or `unreadable` records remain, and every `drifted` record is currently `settled` (`stand-behind`). (2) **Unreadable, unattributed, and already-attributable records are refused**: a record naming no authority (`unattributed`) or whose authority/date cannot be read (`unreadable`) cannot be papered over by human attestation. (3) **Subsequent live-matrix drift turns an earlier settlement `stale`**: each act freezes `underAuthorityIds` from today's live matrix (`pay` for merit cycles, `performance` / line authority for decisions and memos); if a later reorganisation or line change shifts the live holder set (`!sortedIdsEqual(act.underAuthorityIds, currentAuthority.underAuthorityIds)`), the settlement immediately reads `stale` rather than carrying over to a new manager who never signed off. (4) **Contested or multi-principal live authority refuses unilateral peer sign-off**: neither competing line holder may sign off on a peer's behalf; `canSettleAuthority` requires a common DAG ancestor above all live holders, and `RULE-ACR-01` routes to a unique `matrixJointApex` while refusing to guess on matrix diamond ties (`ambiguousApexN`) or `unowned` rights. (5) **Referral is a finding, not standing confirmation**: `authorityReaffirmRefer` opens a linked follow-up case (`createCaseRecord` + typed `informs` provenance edge), marks the row `referred`, closes any open drift-settlement task, and withholds `reconciledClaim` until the reopened matter is re-decided.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **CEO / C-suite primary 220** (last primary 217 — the rotation Session 219 named); director / VP 219; frontline / mid-manager 218. **Structure: single-chain 1–188; MATRIX primary 189–198, 200, 203, 204, 206, 208, 209, 210, 211, 212, 213, 214, 215, 216, 217, 218, 219 and 220.** Single-chain unchanged: automatic post-commit propagation (`RULE-ACR-01`) is inert unless `hasMatrix` is true or the operator explicitly invokes `authorityContinuityScan`. Next rotation: **frontline / mid-manager × matrix** (last primary 218), with period-ledger consumer wiring and the matrix read-model parity audit still In Progress.

**Verified (one focused pass).** `node --test tests/app/authority-reaffirmation.test.mjs tests/app/authority-continuity.test.mjs` — **30/30 PASS**: v129 → v130 migration to empty ledgers and fail-closed normalizer rejection of malformed settlements; `stand-behind` preserving `verdict === 'drifted'` and `populationClaim === false` while granting `reconciledClaim === true` once complete; refusals on `unreadable`, `unattributed`, `attributable`, short reason, and peer seats; live-matrix home-line move turning an earlier settlement `stale`; contested multi-line authority refusing unilateral line-holder sign-off and requiring a joint matrix principal, plus `refer-reopen` creating a linked follow-up case (`informs`) while keeping `reconciledClaim === false`; `RULE-ACR-01` 1:1 spine/contract parity (`100 = 100`), idempotent reconciliation task issuance, automatic closure on settlement, and refusal to guess on a matrix diamond tie (`ambiguousApexN === 1`); and interactive JSDOM settlement click → real serialized reload (`display == stored`), scoped seat withholding of outside-span settler names (`decidedByWithheld === true`), and identity-free CSV #117 + brief verification. Adjacent suites re-run across schema, CSV, seat/router, and matrix contracts (`core`, `csv`, `assessment-reconciliation`, `line-exit`, `line-period-allocation`, `line-reaffirmation`, `matrix-line-consent`, `merit-parity`, `merit-structure`, `onboarding-matrix`, `review-stewardship`, `role-clarity`, `structure-history`, `altitude-router`, `matrix-accountability`) — **all PASS** (`SCHEMA_VERSION` pin moved `129 → 130` in 13 suites; stale `CSV_EXPORTS.length` pin `117 → 118` repaired in `merit-parity` and `role-clarity`, zero assertions weakened). `./node_modules/.bin/eslint` on changed files **PASS (0 errors)**; `npm run check:boundary` and `npm run check:links` **PASS**.

**Unverified / limits.** Full 208-suite `npm test` **[UNVERIFIED]**; `LeadOS-standalone.html` rebuild and a real-browser assistive-technology walkthrough **[UNVERIFIED]**. Settlement binds against **today's** live matrix (`buildMatrix`) because historical `reportingLines` as-of projection remains gated by the Session 207 In Progress blocker; `unreadable` and `unattributed` records deliberately remain un-settleable until historical coverage or source attribution is repaired. Seats remain workflow declarations, not authentication. No implementation blocker.

**New gap discovered (Step 3), added to Planned.** **Matrix Managerial Span Fragmentation & Counterpart-Dyad Coordination Load Ledger** [frontline / mid-manager / director / VP / CEO × matrix]: `spanCalibration.js` prices headcount (`N`) on a single reporting tree, treating a manager whose 8 reports all share 1 counterpart project manager ($k = 1$ negotiation partner) identically to a manager whose 8 reports scatter across 7 distinct secondary lines ($k = 7$ lateral coordination dyads). Grounded in Ocasio (1997) attention-based view, Garicano (2000) knowledge hierarchies, Graicunas (1933) cross-relationship scaling, and Bartlett & Ghoshal (1990) matrix coordination load; would compute exact counterpart-manager count, active cross-line dyad count, and exact rational inverse-HHI counterpart dispersion per seat without person scores or auto-restructuring, refusing spans with incomplete line allocations rather than treating undeclared shares as zero load. Distinct from `spanCalibration.js` (tree headcount), ADR-0140/0158 (per-person capacity shares), and DSM/SCC (work-edge dependency cycles). Repository-wide absence **[UNVERIFIED]**.

## 2026-11-10 — What the quarter actually consumed, not what today charges: Matrix Line Period-Allocation Ledger (Session 219, Schema v129 unchanged, [ADR-0158](./docs/adr/0158-matrix-line-period-allocation.md), CSV #119, `#/matrix?panel=allocation`)

**Implemented — director / VP PRIMARY × matrix; CEO / C-suite read the same board as a portfolio figure; frontline / mid-manager see their own lines through the same seat-scoped read; single-chain supported and inert.** The real duty: the quarter closed, and Priya's line ran four months of it at 40% of Sam and two at 15% after the retune. Every roll-up in the product reads ONE share — the number on the declaration today — so the quarter is priced at 15% everywhere, the 40% months are charged nowhere, and the mid-quarter retune silently re-priced the whole period the day it happened. The budget, capacity and merit readings that consume the share cannot reconcile to the time the person actually spent under each line. This was the exact gap Session 218 entered into Planned for this rotation.

**Built.** One bounded pure read model (`linePeriodAllocation.js` + `linePeriodAllocationRegistry.js`), one panel and one aggregate CSV scope — NO schema move, NO collection, NO stored field, NO rule, NO action: everything printed is derived on read from records the workspace ALREADY stores (each declaration's own window plus the ADR-0140 bounded in-row change history, which nothing had ever read). For a NAMED period the ledger produces the time-weighted charge per declared line in exact integer **share-days** (whole hundredths of a person × whole days), linked at each retune boundary after the time-weighted-return pattern of investment performance measurement (GIPS; Bacon 2013) and the measured-driver logic of activity-based costing (Kaplan & Cooper 1988). Six row states and five person verdicts with declared precedence, the segments each share stood at, both averages printed as numerator ÷ denominator arithmetic, and a per-day **over-commitment floor** — the days on which one person's declared additional lines charged more than a whole person between them, with the worst day printed. The period itself is an input and is validated or refused: two readable days, start ≤ end, a declared 1–731-day bound, never clamped and never swapped; with no period named the default is the LAST COMPLETED calendar quarter and the report says so.

**The refusals are the product.** (1) **A period reaching behind the coverage the retained history can PROVE is refused** with the coverage start and the unprovable day count printed: at the cap of five, retained entries cannot distinguish exactly-five changes from nine-with-four-displaced, and today's share is never projected backwards over the gap — below the cap, coverage is proven to the declaration's own first day. (2) **One undeclared share-day refuses the row's whole total**, one refused row refuses the person, one refused person refuses the workspace, and a refused kind total exports BLANK with its reason: no partial sum ever prints as a whole. (3) **A line the matrix engine refused is never weighted** — the engine's own defect and detail are printed, not paraphrased, and rows naming no roster person are counted as engine refusals and never become person rows. (4) **The home line's allocation is counted out of scope and never weighed**: the pointer moves, its history is ADR-0149's and its as-of reading is ADR-0155's — weighting it here would charge a past period to whoever holds the pointer TODAY, and a person whose only declaration is a home allocation is not in the ledger's population at all. (5) **The over-commitment day claim is made only from a COMPLETE sweep** — where any in-window line could not be priced the claim is refused rather than narrowed, fail-closed in the direction that cannot flatter, and the home line's absence makes the count a printed FLOOR. (6) Two identities are printed as SEPARATE claims (`countsReconcile`, `totalsReconcile`): the state counts add to the printed row count, and the person totals add to the printed workspace total — "the figures add up" and "the total is the sum of the rows printed" are never collapsed into one reassuring word. Declared conventions are printed wherever they touch a figure: the retune day closes at the new share; same-day and out-of-order histories are read in timestamp order and say so; two declared kinds to one manager are one relationship in the graph but TWO charges on the person, both weighed with the merge printed.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **director / VP primary 219** (last primary 216 — the rotation Session 218 named); frontline / mid-manager 218; CEO / C-suite 217. **Structure: single-chain 1–188; MATRIX primary 189–198, 200, 203, 204, 206, 208, 209, 210, 211, 212, 213, 214, 215, 216, 217, 218 and 219.** Single-chain unchanged: no second line reads **empty** with the reason printed — no row, no figure, no refusal, no export row beyond the summary that says so. Next rotation: **CEO / C-suite × matrix** (last primary 217), with the matrix read-model parity audit still In Progress.

**Verified (one focused pass).** `node --test tests/app/line-period-allocation.test.mjs` — **20/20 PASS**: the default period is the last completed quarter and is named as the default; reversed, unreadable and out-of-bounds windows are refused whole-report, never clamped; a steady share weighs to the exact integer (40 × 92 = 3680 share-days) with its segment and identities; a mid-period retune time-weights at the boundary (30 × 45 + 15 × 47 = 2055) and NEITHER today's number nor the old one reproduces it; an ended line is charged for the days it ran and a mid-period start only from its start; an out-of-window line is counted and blocks nothing; a capped history refuses the reaching-back period with the coverage start and 31 unprovable days printed, computes the period inside the coverage, and proves coverage to the first day below the cap; an undeclared stretch refuses the row with the day count; an engine-refused line is never weighted and a roster-missing row never becomes a person; the home allocation is counted out of scope and a home-only person is not in the population; over-commitment counts 92 days at 130% and is REFUSED from a partial sweep; two kinds to one manager both weigh with the merge flag on exactly one row; same-day retunes close at the last value and out-of-order history is read in timestamp order, both printed; the seat scope withholds and counts two people from a product seat while the operator sees all; a single-chain workspace is inert end to end with the schema pinned unmoved at v129; a **real-API declare → retune → weigh round trip** lands exactly where the day sweep says, with **display == stored across a real reload** (persisted history entry and current share asserted against the printed first/last day), the read writing no byte and bumping no revision; the export is exact-column, aggregate-only (identity audit over every banned string including note text), reconciles cell-for-cell with the board, and refuses BLANK-with-reason at workspace and kind level; the brief names nobody and prints the total and the identity claim; and a JSDOM render of `#/matrix?panel=allocation` prints every modelled row cell-for-cell (person, weight, state), the board total with its denominator, the retune banner and the refused-window banner, mutating nothing. Adjacent suites re-run because the CSV register, the matrix panel list, the matrix view and the axe route list all moved: `csv` + `merit-structure` + `matrix-accountability` + `matrix-governance` + `line-reaffirmation` + `rights-concordance` + `authority-continuity` + `workspace-navigation` + `core` **141/141**; `access-audit` **14/14** with the new route axe-clean; the `CSV_EXPORTS.length` pin moved 117 → 118 in `csv` and `merit-structure` — no assertion was relaxed. `npx eslint` on the changed files **PASS (0 errors)**; `npm run check:boundary` **PASS** (664 app ES modules, 207 suites, 23 doc checks, 0 leaks).

**Unverified / limits.** Full 207-suite `npm test` **[UNVERIFIED]**; `LeadOS-standalone.html` rebuild and a real-browser assistive-technology walkthrough of the new panel **[UNVERIFIED]** (the route was added to the axe list and the JSDOM suite ran it; the browser run itself did not). The ledger prices the DECLARED side of a period: an allocation remains a declaration, not a measurement (ADR-0140's own limit), and share-days are not evidence of hours worked. The over-commitment floor excludes the home line, so a day total below 100% is not a claim the remainder was free. The budget/capacity/merit consumers still read today's single share; wiring them through the period ledger is the recorded remainder below, deliberately not this slice. Upstream import/normalisation retention of `history` beyond the normalizer is not re-certified by this slice. Seats remain workflow declarations, not authentication. No implementation blocker.

**New gap discovered (Step 3), added to Planned.** **Matrix allocation-to-output reconciliation — declared share-days against observed work landings [BLOCKED — needs line attribution on work records; see Session 221]** [director / VP / CEO × matrix]: this session prices what each line was DECLARED to consume over a period; nothing compares it to what actually landed. The engine already computes per-line work reach (`matrixWorkReach`), so a 40% line that received one twentieth of the person's completed work in the same window is visible nowhere — it is either a lagging declaration or misrouted work, and activity-based costing exists precisely because declared bases drift from observed consumption. Would join the #119 share-day numerators to per-line work-item counts and closes inside the SAME named window, print both sides with their windows, and REFUSE the comparison where either side is incomplete (an unpriced line or items whose line reach cannot be resolved) rather than comparing a part to a whole; never a rating of a person and never an automatic retune. Distinct from ADR-0140 (point-in-time balance), ADR-0146 (recurring decision-bypass signatures) and ADR-0158 (the declared side only). Repository-wide absence **[UNVERIFIED]**. Also recorded **In Progress**: the period-ledger consumer wiring (budget span, capacity and merit reading their period figures through the share-day ledger), plus the standing matrix read-model parity audit, two-sided re-affirmation on an ADR-0148 consent row, and the merit remainder.

## 2026-11-10 — A line agreed in 2023 is still charged in 2026: Matrix Line Re-Affirmation (Session 218, Schema v129, [ADR-0157](./docs/adr/0157-matrix-line-reaffirmation.md), `RULE-LRF-01`, CSV #118, `#/matrix?panel=renewal`)

**Implemented — frontline / mid-manager PRIMARY × matrix; director, VP and the C-suite read the same lens; single-chain supported and inert.** The real duty: Priya has held 40% of Sam since September 2023, her project finished in 2024, and the share is still charged to Sam every single day — because a declaration stands until a human ends it, and nobody ever put the question back to either of them. ADR-0148 made a declared share an **ask** with a window; ADR-0152 read the work an **ended** line left behind. Neither gave a line a **term of office**, and neither gave either side a dated way to say *this no longer holds*. So the product could say a line was agreed once, and could not say what anyone agrees to **today**.

**Built.** One bounded read model (`lineReaffirmation.js` + `lineReaffirmationRegistry.js` + fail-closed `lineReaffirmationSchema.js`), four commands, one rule, one panel and one aggregate CSV scope. A declared line now has a term: the manager who **holds** the line re-affirms it (at the share it currently carries, for a term they state) or **releases** it with a stated reason; the person whose hours are taken **accepts** or **objects** in their own words. Eight derived line states and ten person verdicts with declared precedence, so the rule, the panel, the brief and the CSV cannot disagree about a word. Nothing derived is stored; the answer row keeps the share it was given for, and the declaration is read live on every render.

**The refusals are the product.** (1) **A release does not end the charge.** The declaration stands, the ledger keeps charging the share, the receipt prints `stillCharged` and the percentage, and the register counts released-but-charged lines separately — ending a line stays the governed `matrixEndLine`, because an engine that quietly subtracted a released share would report capacity no declaration supports, and one that ended lines would be silently removing accountability. (2) **An objection is a finding, not a resolution.** It is recorded, counted, and escalated to that person's **home line** — ending somebody else's accountability is the line manager's act, not the informed party's. (3) **A lapsed term is never renewed by arithmetic**, and a renewal with no end date is **dropped at load** with a printed warning: it cannot be told apart from one nobody revisited. (4) **A changed share is not a re-affirmed share** — a line retuned after the answer reads `changed-share` with both numbers printed. (5) A re-affirmation past 100% of a person is refused **with the arithmetic printed** (`70% + 40% = 110% of Sam`), and the check is refused rather than guessed when any share is undeclared. (6) An undeclared line **refuses both share totals outright** with its reason instead of printing a partial sum. The board's two integers — share covered by a **live re-affirmed term** and share charged with **no live answer** — are printed apart, with their sum to the declared total printed as a **claim** (`reconciles`), and answers dated in the future are counted and never read as in force. `RULE-LRF-01` puts one owned, dated ask in front of the line holder for `no-term` / `term-lapsed` / `reaffirmation-due` / `changed-share`, one in front of the **person** once a renewal has stood past its window unanswered, one in front of the person's **home line** on an objection, and one in front of the manager for a released line still charging a share; typed provenance only, capped with the remainder counted and retried by the scan, inert in a single chain.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **frontline / mid-manager primary 218** (last primary 214 — the rotation Session 217 named); director / VP 216; CEO / C-suite 217. **Structure: single-chain 1–188; MATRIX primary 189–198, 200, 203, 204, 206, 208, 209, 210, 211, 212, 213, 214, 215, 216, 217 and 218.** Single-chain unchanged: a workspace with no second line reads **empty** with the reason printed — no row, no term, no ask, no edge, no rule. Next rotation: **director / VP × matrix** (last primary 216), with the matrix read-model parity audit still In Progress.

**Verified (one focused pass).** `node --test tests/app/line-reaffirmation.test.mjs` — **19/19 PASS**: no stored answer reads `no-term` and is never read as in-term; a live term both sides answered reads `in-term` while a term that ran out reads `lapsed` **and stays charged**; a retuned share prints both numbers and refuses to cover the line; a release records a decision and **never** ends the charge, with the declaration left byte-identical; an objection is a finding that outranks a due window and does not end anything; the warning window, and a future-dated answer that is **counted and not read as in force**; an undeclared share refuses both totals and exports BLANK with the reason; a re-affirmation past 100% is refused with the arithmetic; the seat rules (only the line's manager re-affirms or releases, only the person answers) and the date/reason validations; a **real-API round trip** re-affirm → person accepts → release, with `stillCharged` on the receipt and the declaration untouched; the rule's four routing cases through the real `matrixDeclareLine` action and a scan; **display == stored across a real reload** with every printed person/line cell asserted against the persisted declaration and the recomputed blob, both identities printed, reads mutating nothing and bumping no revision; the export is aggregate-only with an identity audit and reconciles to the panel; the brief names nobody; a single-chain workspace is inert; the vocabulary is closed and refused rows are dropped at load with warnings. Adjacent suites re-run because the schema, the seat rights, the gateway, the rule list, the panel list and the CSV register all moved: `core` + `csv` + `matrix-line-consent` + `matrix-term-exposure` + `matrix-governance` + `rights-concordance` + `structure-history` + `line-exit` + `review-stewardship` + `onboarding-matrix` + `role-clarity` **150/150**. `npx eslint` on the changed files **PASS (0 errors)**; `npm run check:boundary` **PASS** (661 app ES modules, 206 suites, 23 doc checks, 0 leaks); rule/contract parity on the shared spine **99 = 99**.

**Unverified / limits.** Full 206-suite `npm test` **[UNVERIFIED]**; `LeadOS-standalone.html` rebuild and a real-browser assistive-technology walkthrough of the new panel **[UNVERIFIED]**. A workspace that upgrades reads **every** line as `no-term` — the honest reading, and it will look worse than yesterday until somebody answers, which the panel and the brief both state. The register covers DECLARED additional lines only; the home line's own history is ADR-0149's. Releasing a line records a decision and deliberately does **not** date the declaration out, so the charge survives until a human runs the governed End action. Seats remain workflow declarations, not authentication. No implementation blocker.

**New gap discovered (Step 3), added to Planned.** **Matrix line fractional-period allocation accounting** [director / VP / CEO × matrix]: this session gives a line a term and a decision about whether it continues, but every share in the product is a single number read for *today*. A line that ran four months of a twelve-month year at 40% then six at 15% is charged 15% in every roll-up and 40% in none, so the budget, capacity and merit readings that consume the share cannot reconcile to the time the person actually spent under each line — and a mid-cycle retune silently re-prices the whole period. Would read each declaration's own window plus its stored share history (already bounded on the row by ADR-0140) as a **time-weighted** share per period, print the period the share was in force for, and REFUSE the weighted figure where a line's history does not cover the window asked about rather than projecting today's number backwards. Distinct from ADR-0142's envelope exposure (a point-in-time position per currency), ADR-0154/0155's merit cohort reads (a pay decision, not a capacity period) and this session's term (whether the line continues, not what it consumed). Repository-wide absence **[UNVERIFIED]**. Also recorded **In Progress**: the line sunset remainder is now closed by this session, but the matrix read-model parity audit, two-sided re-affirmation on an ADR-0148 consent row (still not back-filled), and the merit remainder remain open.

## 2026-11-10 — The board asked about the portfolio: Matrix Authority Continuity (Session 217, Schema v128 unchanged, [ADR-0156](./docs/adr/0156-matrix-authority-continuity.md), CSV #117, `#/matrix?panel=continuity`)

**Implemented — CEO / C-suite PRIMARY × matrix; director / VP and mid-manager read the same lens; single-chain supported and inert.** The real duty: the board asks the **portfolio** question — *are our frozen decisions still attributable to the authority that made them?* — and the product could answer it for exactly ONE decision type. A finalised merit cycle now proves its own structure (ADR-0155). A decided decision record and a committed board memo cannot reproduce their own authority at all, and a March pricing decision naming a CFO who has since left reads *complete and clear* in a pack nobody re-checks. A chief does not hold one kind of frozen decision; they hold a portfolio of them, so the surface had to read the portfolio.

**Built.** One bounded read model (`authorityContinuity.js` + `authorityContinuityRegistry.js`), one panel and one aggregate CSV scope. It reads the frozen decision records the workspace **already stores** — a finalised merit cycle, a decided decision record, a committed/frozen/superseded board memo — and compares each record's **own** authority against the authority in force on that record's **own day**, read through the SAME as-of structure engine (ADR-0155) over the SAME matrix engine (ADR-0140). The merit type reuses ADR-0155's own `compareFrozenStructure` contract verbatim, so the two modules can never disagree about whether a cycle drifted. **Two claims, never collapsed:** *covered agreement* (do the records we CAN compare still name the authority in force?) and the *portfolio claim* (may that be asserted of the whole population?). The portfolio claim is **REFUSED** whenever the covered population is below the declared floor of 3, whenever any covered record did not agree, or whenever **any record could not be read** — an absence is the one thing a continuity claim must never absorb (population completeness, AICPA AU-C 500). **Four verdicts:** `attributable`, `drifted` (a STRUCTURE MOVED UNDER A DECISION — never that the decision was wrong), `unattributed` (the record names nobody and is never filled in), `unreadable` (counted, printed with its reason, never dropped). **Two comparison routes and the route used is PRINTED:** `subject` (the subject resolved through a typed edge — a link to a `person`, or a link to a `case` whose `ownerId` is the person; a subject is NEVER guessed from the approver's own span) and `span` (no resolvable subject, so the approver must have been a manager with reports on that date — a WEAKER reading, and the row says so). The rights are the **real RAPID vocabulary** (`pay` for a cycle, `performance` for an approval): an invented right name would compare against nothing and every record would read `drifted`, which is a false alarm in the alarming direction. **Report, never correct:** a drifted record is named, the frozen record is never edited to match today and today's reading is never overwritten to agree. No person is scored; no manager is invented; the export carries counts, verdicts and the claim reason and never a record id, title, person id, manager id, name or the date of any individual decision; and the **authority NAME is scoped** the way the concordance module scopes it — a record in scope because it concerns someone in the seat's span but naming an authority outside it prints `outside this seat`, with the verdict and the counts untouched. No stored derived figure, no new collection, no rule, no second hierarchy, no schema bump.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **CEO / C-suite primary 217** (last primary 215, the rotation Sessions 216 and 217 both named); director / VP 216; frontline / mid-manager 214. **Structure: single-chain 1–188; MATRIX primary 189–198, 200, 203, 204, 206, 208, 209, 210, 211, 212, 213, 214, 215, 216 and 217.** Single-chain unchanged: a workspace with no frozen decision records reads **empty** with the claim refused and the reason printed — no row, no ask, no edge, no rule. Next rotation: **frontline / mid-manager × matrix** (last primary 214), with the matrix read-model parity audit and the merit remainder still In Progress.

**Verified (one focused pass).** `node --test tests/app/authority-continuity.test.mjs` — **23/23 PASS**: the register reads every frozen decision type and not only the easy one; a decision is compared against the authority on its **own** day, not today's; a decision whose approver did not hold the line on that day reads `drifted`; a record whose authority cannot be read is **counted** and refuses the portfolio claim; the claim is refused below the declared floor; a complete population grants it; a record that names no authority is `unattributed` and never filled in; a record whose subject cannot be resolved falls back to the approver's span and PRINTS that it did so; an approver who managed nobody on the record's own day reads `drifted`; the register writes nothing (the state is byte-identical after a read); every printed figure equals the recomputed blob after a **real reload**; the verdict counts and the type buckets reconcile to the population; the export carries no identity; the registered CSV scope carries the same figures as the panel; the brief names nobody; a single-chain workspace with no frozen decisions reads empty rather than broken; an authority **outside the seat's span is withheld** while its verdict and the counts survive; the schema is unchanged; and a **JSDOM render** prints the computed claim reason and refuses an incomplete population. **The cross-module integration is proven through the REAL API:** a merit cycle finalised through the actual `finalizeMeritCycle` action — which freezes the structure block beside the money — enters the register and is compared through ADR-0155's own `compareFrozenStructure` contract, so the two modules cannot disagree; a home-line move effective AFTER the cycle does **not** drift the record (a later move cannot unmake the decision), and a move recorded AFTER the freeze but effective BEFORE the cycle **does** drift it, with the frozen block left byte-identical. Adjacent suites re-run because the CSV registry, the panel list, the matrix view and the accessibility route list all moved: `merit-structure` + `csv` + `matrix-accountability` + `matrix-governance` **53/53**. `npx eslint` on the changed files **PASS (0 errors)**; `npm run check:boundary` **PASS** (655 app ES modules, 205 suites, 23 doc checks, 0 leaks); `npm run check:links` **PASS** (1013 links across 274 markdown files).

**Unverified / limits.** Full 205-suite `npm test` **[UNVERIFIED]**; `LeadOS-standalone.html` rebuild and a real-browser assistive-technology walkthrough of the new panel **[UNVERIFIED]** (the route was added to the axe list, but the axe run itself was not executed this session). This slice reads the **record's own stored authority**; it does NOT back-fill a `structure` block into the decision log or the board memo, so a pre-existing record of those types is compared against the as-of structure rather than against a frozen block of its own — the comparison is honest, but it is a comparison against the RECORDED history, not against a snapshot the record itself carries. The `span` fallback route is deliberately weaker than the `subject` route and says so on every row that uses it. Upstream import/normalisation retention of the frozen blocks is not certified by this slice. Seats remain workflow declarations, not authentication. No implementation blocker.

## 2026-11-10 — The packet named the wrong manager: As-Of Home-Line Authority & Frozen Structure (Session 216, Schema v128 unchanged, [ADR-0155](./docs/adr/0155-as-of-home-line-authority.md), frozen snapshot v1 → v2, CSV #116 extended, `#/merit?panel=matrix`)

**Implemented — director / VP PRIMARY × matrix; CEO / C-suite and mid-manager read the same lens; single-chain supported and inert.** The real duty: the merit cycle was finalised in November and Sam was paid 2.5% under Dana's `pay` right. In February the reorganisation moved Sam's home line to Marcus. In March an auditor opens the November packet and asks the only question that matters about it — *who held the pay right when this money landed?* Every matrix surface in the product answered from `person.managerId`, today's pointer, so the packet credited Marcus with a decision he had never seen. And nothing anywhere said the answer had changed, because the frozen `audit` carried band integrity, the decomposition and the departure predictions and **no structure at all**. A frozen decision record that cannot reproduce the authority in force on its own effective date does not support the decision (COSO 2013 control activities; IIA evidence sufficiency), and the failure was silent in the worst direction: the packet read *complete and clear* with the wrong manager's name on it.

**Built.** One read model (`meritStructure.js` + `meritStructureRegistry.js`), one frozen block on the existing cycle row, and the existing merit-parity reader routed through it. **Four states, never collapsed:** `observed` (a recorded period covers the day — including a CLOSED period that reaches a future day, because reading a declared end date is reading a declaration), `projected` (an OPEN period read for a day that has not happened: the line is presumed to continue), `presumed-current` (no recorded home-line history at all, so today's pointer is a PRINTED PRESUMPTION — the one reading that keeps every existing workspace's merit page working), and `unrecorded` (records exist for this person and NONE reaches the day: an absence that BLOCKS). A joiner who did not exist yet is a fifth fact, counted separately. The as-of reading substitutes each person's home pointer and runs the **same** `buildMatrix` engine at the as-of day — one hierarchy, not two — and the engine's own refusals against the as-of graph are counted and printed rather than dropped. **The refusals are the product:** an unreadable home line reads `authorityState: 'unknown'` — never `unowned`, never cleared from today's roster — is excluded with a named reason, and withholds the cohort medians, the gap and the pool share through the *existing* complete-pool gate rather than narrowing the sample quietly; it also forces `figuresComplete: false`, because a structure claim the record cannot support is not a complete reading. **Freeze beside the money:** `finalizeMeritCycle` builds the structure block in the SAME transaction as the status change, carrying the effective date read for, the capture day, the ledger's coverage start, the four state counts, the supersession count, the pool as read that day, and one `{personId, state, managerId}` row per person — no new disclosure, since the cycle already stores `predictions` keyed by `personId`. **Compare, report, never correct:** four declared verdicts `not-frozen` → `unreadable` → `drifted` → `identical`; `drifted` names which people moved and which structure figure is no longer reproduced, the frozen record is never edited to match today and the live reading is never overwritten to agree — and there is no fifth verdict in which an absent comparison silently passes. No second hierarchy, no stored derived figure, no correction command, no rule (a rule reacting to drift would open work about money already paid). CSV scope #116 gains eleven count-only columns and still carries no manager id, manager name or person id.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **director / VP primary 216** (last primary 213, the target Sessions 213–215 named); CEO / C-suite 215; frontline / mid-manager 214. **Structure: single-chain 1–188; MATRIX primary 189–198, 200, 203, 204, 206, 208, 209, 210, 211, 212, 213, 214, 215 and 216.** Single-chain unchanged: no ledger substitution is made, every figure is byte-identical to the pre-ADR-0155 reading, and the tab prints the presumption so a reader knows why. Next rotation: **CEO / C-suite × matrix** (last primary 215), with the matrix read-model parity audit and the merit remainder still In Progress.

**Verified (one focused pass, two corrections).** `node --test tests/app/merit-structure.test.mjs` — **17/17 PASS**: a home line that moved AFTER the effective date is read as it stood on that day with both managers printed; a home line that moved BEFORE it is already the new manager; an unrecorded home line reads UNKNOWN, is excluded, withholds the gap and forces `figuresComplete: false`; a future effective date reads `projected` and never `observed`; a workspace with no recorded history is inert and byte-identical with the presumption printed; a person who had not started is the fifth fact; finalising freezes the effective-date structure beside the money; a post-finalisation move reads `drifted` with the frozen record untouched; a v1 snapshot reads `not-frozen` (an absence, not a match); a frozen row that cannot be read is dropped AND counted; every printed structure figure equals the recomputed blob across a real reload with reads mutating nothing; CSV #116 carries the new counts with no manager or person identity; the vocabulary is closed and the states reconcile by construction; no cycle prints a printed absence; the panel prints the as-of structure, both managers, the supersession and the withheld gap, in a JSDOM render. **Two defects found by the first run and fixed in place (not test relaxations):** (1) an OPEN period was being reported `projected` for a *closed* record — the logic now distinguishes a declared end date (reading a declaration) from an open period extrapolated forward (a presumption), which had been mislabelling every future-dated cycle; (2) `compareFrozenStructure` compared the frozen **pay-row** count against the **roster** count, so every cycle would have read `drifted` — a false alarm in the reassuring direction's mirror image; it now compares only structure figures. Adjacent suites, re-run because the merit reader, `compSchema` and the CSV columns all moved: `merit-parity` **25/25**, `structure-history` + `csv` PASS. `merit-equity` shows the **pre-existing stale-pin class** recorded in the baseline (schema pin 119 against 128, CSV pin 104 against 115) — neither caused by this change and neither touched. `npm run lint` PASS (changed files, 0 errors); `npm run check:boundary` PASS (652 app ES modules, 204 suites, 23 doc checks, 0 leaks).

**Unverified / limits.** Full 204-suite `npm test` **[UNVERIFIED]**; `LeadOS-standalone.html` rebuild and a real-browser assistive-technology walkthrough **[UNVERIFIED]**. This slice reads the HOME line historically; historical reconstruction of *declared* (non-home) lines beyond their stored windows is not certified, because they already carry their own windows through `periodLinesFor`. Upstream import/normalisation retention of `structureHistory` is not certified by this slice. The adjusted Oaxaca–Blinder screening and the cross-line review-evidence join remain In Progress under ADR-0154. Seats remain workflow declarations, not authentication. No implementation blocker.

**New gap discovered (Step 3), added to Planned.** **A matrix authority continuity register across the whole frozen-decision set — which decisions are still attributable to the authority that made them, and which have drifted** [director / VP / CEO × matrix]: this session makes ONE frozen decision type (merit) able to prove its own structure, and the comparison is per cycle on one screen. Nothing audits the *portfolio*: a director has merit cycles, priority arbitrations, line consents, review packets and budget releases each frozen under a structure, and no surface says which of them still reproduce the authority they were decided under and which now name managers who never held the line. Would run the same `compareFrozenStructure` contract over every module that freezes a decision, aggregate by altitude and by decision type, and refuse a portfolio-level "all attributable" claim wherever any module has no `structure` block to compare — an absence being the one thing a continuity claim must never absorb. Distinct from ADR-0149 (stored acts against their own day) and ADR-0155 (one decision type, one cycle). Repository-wide absence **[UNVERIFIED]**.

## 2026-11-10 — The pool read "inside budget, no finding" while the second-line people were paid differently: Matrix Merit Pool Stewardship & Cohort Parity (Session 212, Schema v128 unchanged, [ADR-0154](./docs/adr/0154-matrix-merit-pool-parity.md), CSV #116, `#/merit?panel=matrix`)

**Implemented — CEO / C-suite PRIMARY × matrix; director / VP read the same lens; single-chain fully supported and inert.** The real duty: it is the first week of November and the merit pool is being finalised. Sam sits on two lines — Dana's functional team, which sets pay, and Priya's migration programme, whose declaration also carries the `pay` right because a pay decision without the delivery manager in the room was always wrong. Nobody has ever put the two declarations beside a pay decision. The cycle reads *inside budget, no finding*; Sam receives 2.5% while the rest of Dana's team receives 4%; and there is no surface in the product that says either that **the authority which set that number was not attributable** or that **the people carrying a second line were paid differently from the people who were not**. Holmström & Milgrom (1991) multi-task agency explains the mechanism — with two principals each observing part of the output, effort follows the task whose principal can reward it and the unrewarded one is starved by the measurement, not by a person — and Baker, Gibbons & Murphy (1994) explain why review never caught it: pay attached to a supervisor who sees part of the job prices the part they see.

**Built.** No new collection, no stored field, no rule, no schema version. One bounded read model (`meritParity.js` + `meritParityRegistry.js`) over records the workspace already stores — the cycle, the roster, the DATED `reportingLines` and completed reviews for composition — and one panel on the existing merit terminal. **Two claims, printed apart, never collapsed** (NORTH_STAR Bulletproof Reliability): **authority** (`unknown` → `unowned` → `contested` → `clear`: how many declared lines held the `pay` right for each person being paid on the effective date) and **parity** (`no-cycle` → `single-line` → `incomplete` → `divergent` → `parity`: whether the second-line cohort received a different median increase in basis points than the home-line cohort). The cohort split and the authority are read **on the cycle's own effective date** through `periodLinesFor` — a project line that ended in October does not make a November pay decision matrix, one that starts in December does not either, and one that *was* live does even if it is gone today. Ratings are read as of the effective date and never from the future; the date used is printed. Every figure is exact integer arithmetic: pay in integer cents, increase in whole basis points **truncated with the remainder FLAGGED**, the **lower median** by declared convention, a zero increase read from the CENTS (never from a basis point figure truncation flattened to 0), and the second-line share of the pool in basis points of the pool.

**The refusals are the product.** A declared **cell floor of three priced people per cohort** withholds the medians, the gap and the pool share as BLANK with the reason printed — never a zero, never a two-person anecdote. An unpriced row, a row naming a person off the roster, or a bounded read that hit its cap withholds the gap **entirely** rather than narrowing the sample quietly; a removed person's authority reads `unknown`, never assumed clear. A pool that moved no money cannot read `parity` — a zero gap from an unspent pool is an artefact. The gap is **UNADJUSTED and descriptive**: direction is printed (`matrix-below` / `matrix-above`), a declared ±50 bp band decides the word, and the page says in words that the band is a convention, that fairness was not proven, and that no cause is claimed; a level-matched reading prints only where both cells clear the floor and is still descriptive. **No authority is settled**: there is no control on the panel and no command in the API that picks one of several `pay` holders. `reconciles` (the counts add up) and `figuresComplete` (every printed figure is computed and nothing needed is missing) are two separate claims, so a single-line pool is complete about printing no gap while an `incomplete` pool never is. CSV #116 is aggregate-only: no person, name, manager id, cycle label, salary or individual increase in any cell, and a withheld figure is BLANK with its reason. Nothing derived is stored, so display == stored by construction. Seat-safe reads registered on the shared boundary.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **CEO / C-suite primary 212** (last primary 198, the longest-unserved matrix-primary altitude); director / VP 211; frontline / mid-manager 210. **Structure: single-chain 1–188; MATRIX primary 189–198, 200, 203, 204, 206, 208, 209, 210, 211 and 212.** Single-chain unchanged: no second-line cohort, no gap, no finding — the tab states that no fairness claim has been made. Next rotation: **director / VP × matrix**, with the matrix read-model parity audit and the new merit remainder still In Progress.

**Verified (one focused pass).** `node --test tests/app/merit-parity.test.mjs` — **20/20 PASS**: the cohort split is read on the effective date (ended line, future line, live line); a second line declaring `pay` reads `contested` with both holders named; a home line with an unaided declaration still reads `clear`; a pay row naming a person off the roster is excluded and reads `unknown`, blocking the gap; basis points are exact integers from cents with truncation flagged and a truncated 0 does not become a zero increase; the lower median is the declared convention and the gap is exact; a below-floor cohort withholds median and gap as BLANK with the reason; one unpriced row counts, excludes and blocks the comparison rather than reading as a zero increase; a pool that moved no money cannot read `parity`; a divergence prints its direction and claims no cause; an inside-band gap reads `parity` with "fairness was not proven"; a single-line pool is inert and complete about printing no gap; level-matched cells print only above the floor; **display == stored** across a real reload with every total equal to the recomputed blob and reads mutating nothing and bumping no revision; CSV #116 registered (115 scopes), exact-column, aggregate-only, reconciling with the panel and exporting a withheld figure BLANK with its reason; the declared vocabulary is closed (floor 3, band 50 bp, the two ladders and their precedence); a workspace with no cycle returns a printed `no-cycle` report rather than an empty pool; and a JSDOM render prints both verdicts, the −2.00% gap, the contested authority, the holders, the reconciliation claims and the frameworks, plus a below-floor workspace printing `withheld` rather than a number. Adjacent suites, re-run because the CSV register and the merit view moved: `csv` + `role-clarity` **23/23** (pins corrected 114 → 115); `merit-equity` 13/17 and `operating-seat`/`terminal-publication` re-run with the **same pre-existing stale-pin class** recorded before this session (schema pins 119/123 against 128, CSV pin 104 against 115, and a date-fragile publish fixture expecting 2026-11-05) — none caused by this change and none touched. `npm run lint` PASS (changed files, 0 errors); `npm run check:boundary` PASS (650 app ES modules, 202 suites, 23 doc checks, 0 leaks).

**Unverified / limits.** Full 202-suite `npm test` **[UNVERIFIED]**; standalone build and a real-browser assistive-technology walkthrough **[UNVERIFIED]**. The reading is unadjusted for level, rating, tenure, performance and market movement — composition columns are printed so the confound the module does not model is visible, not buried. The matrix engine reads the home line from `person.managerId` today, so a home-line move is treated as in force on the effective date unless the declared line's own window says otherwise; the page says so rather than inventing a history. No leave-cycle declaration exists: the reading reports, it never blocks or approves a finalisation. Seats remain workflow declarations, not authentication. No blocker.

**New gap discovered (Step 3), added to Planned below:** **a frozen matrix-merit audit and an as-of home-line authority read — the structure a past pay decision was actually made in** [director / VP / CEO × matrix] — this session reads the cohort split and the pay authority from the DATED declared lines, but the HOME line comes from today's `person.managerId`, and the merit terminal's frozen `audit` snapshot carries band integrity, the decomposition and the departure predictions but **not** the cohort split or the pay-right holders. A home-line move or a re-declaration therefore silently re-reads a past cycle's structure, and a finalised pool cannot prove who held the pay right when the money landed. Would join ADR-0149's dated home-line periods to the matrix engine's home edge (withholding on a day the ledger does not cover rather than projecting today backwards) and freeze the cohort counts, medians and holder counts into the audit snapshot at finalisation, superseded only by a new finalisation. Distinct from ADR-0149 (which reconciles stored acts against their own day and deliberately does not feed the matrix engine) and from ADR-0154 (the live reading). Repository-wide absence **[UNVERIFIED]**.

## 2026-11-09 — Two reasonable sentences that cannot both be served: Cross-Line Role Clarity Reconciliation (Session 211, Schema v128, [ADR-0153](./docs/adr/0153-cross-line-role-clarity.md), CSV #115, `#/onboarding?panel=clarity`)

**Implemented — director / VP PRIMARY × matrix; every altitude reads the same lens; single-chain fully supported and inert.** The real duty: Sam sits on two lines. Dana's brief says she owns the migration end-to-end — `delivery`, `technical`, `risk`, `decides`, `written`. Priya's brief for the same person says support the migration when asked — `delivery` alone, `informed`, no criteria at all. Both briefs are dated, both read as reasonable sentences, and nothing ever put them side by side. Two managers grading the same work against different definitions of good is not a performance problem or a calibration problem — it is a role problem (Kahn et al. 1964), and it is visible before anyone is graded. Session 208 closed *did every line say it expects something*; Session 209 closed *did every line agree about what happened*; this closes the question between them: **did the lines agree what the person was for?**

**Built.** No new collection. Three OPTIONAL, fail-closed marks on the ADR-0150 brief rows (`domains` from a closed ten-tag accountability-domain lexicon, deduplicated and capped; `decisionRight` on a closed three-step RACI-informed scale `decides` 2 / `advises` 1 / `informed` 0; `criteria` on a closed three-step standing `written` 2 / `verbal` 1 / `unstated` 0). Declared **by the line that wrote the brief or not at all**: the write path refuses an unknown domain/right/standing with the closed vocabulary printed, and the loader drops an unknown value with a printed warning — never silently, never coerced. One bounded read model (`roleClarity.js` + `roleClarityRegistry.js`) over the existing briefs, the same `buildMatrix` + `periodLinesFor` path every matrix module uses, and the same seat-checked read path; nothing derived is stored. Comparison is exact integer arithmetic: a domain claimed by ≥2 comparable lines reads `overlapping-scope` (the expected shape of a matrix, always printed), a decision-right spread ≥2 reads `contested-authority`, a criteria spread ≥2 reads `divergent-criteria` — both render the case as `contested`, named **before anyone is graded**. Six verdicts with declared precedence (`unbriefed` → `contested` → `unscoped-pair` → `overlapping` → `partitioned`, plus inert `single-chain`) so the board, the case and the CSV cannot disagree. A SECONDARY line that never briefed fails the case to `unbriefed`; the home line carries the plan as a printed presumption and is never decomposed into domains; a declined line is an answer, never a definition; a brief with no marks is `unscoped-line` and excluded from every comparison, named as such; one-step spreads are notes, never conflicts (the scales are three steps wide — declaring two declares the scale, not a fitted threshold; **there are no conventions to clamp**). Every finding is on a LINE or a DOMAIN — nobody is scored, no per-line share exists, and no conflict is settled by the lens. `RULE-ONB-01` (ADR-0150) already issues the per-unbriefed-line asks; **no rule is added, by design** — a rule that auto-resolved a definition conflict would route work without a human looking at the two definitions.

## 2026-11-09 — The line ended; the work it created did not: Matrix Line-Exit Obligation Register (Session 210, Schema v127, [ADR-0152](./docs/adr/0152-matrix-line-exit-obligations.md), `RULE-LEX-01`, CSV #114, `#/matrix?panel=exit` Reconciliation)

**Implemented — frontline / mid-manager PRIMARY × matrix; every altitude reads the same register; single-chain fully supported and inert.** The real duty: Priya's project line for Sam was dated out on 31 October. The review input ask sent to Priya in February is still open, and Sam never acknowledged the project's onboarding brief. Nothing in the workspace tells a leader whether those asks are still owed by anyone, or whether they are looking at work that structurally cannot close. Every matrix register before this one reads the LIVE line set — consent asks the manager a line was given to, stewardship asks the manager who held the line in a period, onboarding asks the manager who holds the line in a window — so the moment a line is dated out, all of that work keeps its addressee and its roll-up edge while the line that justified it no longer exists.

**Built.** One bounded read model (`lineExit.js`) over the obligations the workspace **already stores** — the unacknowledged line onboarding brief (ADR-0150) and the unanswered review input ask (ADR-0147), the only two records that carry the LINE KEY they were addressed to — matched against the declared lines that have actually ended, plus **one** dated human command per obligation, and one rule on the shared spine. Stored: `lineExitRemedies` — one row per dated act on one obligation (retire with a reason, or carry to a named manager who holds a live line today). `lineExitMarkers` is `RULE-LEX-01`'s idempotency ledger. Derived on every read and never stored: every obligation, state, window verdict, day count, line verdict and total.

**The refusals that are the product.** (1) **Never re-point** — a carry must name a manager who holds a LIVE line for that person today; the person herself, the manager whose line ended and any third party are refused, and the panel's picker offers exactly the set the action accepts. (2) **Never void by arithmetic** — a work window entirely outside the line's life is FLAGGED (`after`), never retired automatically; a side with no dated window reads `unknown`, never the reassuring answer. (3) **Never settle by silence** — an obligation left by an ended line reads `open` with its age in whole days. (4) **Never overwrite an answer** — an obligation the person or the line already answered is not in the register, and a remedy naming it is refused with that reason. (5) **Never invent an end or an heir** — a line key that resolves to nothing reads `vanished`, is counted as unsettled, and issues no work (a task addressed to nobody could never close). (6) **The HOME line is handed over, not adjudicated** — home-keyed obligations are counted, the count that predates a recorded home-line move is printed, and the reader is sent to ADR-0149 rather than given an invented home-line end. (7) A line-consent acknowledgement ask is deliberately **not** read: the generated ask names a person and no line, so the join would be a guess.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **frontline / mid-manager primary 210** (previous primary 209); director / VP 209; CEO / C-suite 198. **Structure: single-chain 1–188; MATRIX primary 189–198, 200, 203, 204, 206, 208, 209 and 210.** Single-chain unchanged: no row, no ask, no edge, no delegation. Next rotation: **director / VP × matrix**, with the matrix read-model parity audit still In Progress.

Standalone build and real-browser assistive-technology walkthrough **[UNVERIFIED]**. A brief carries no due day on the record, so its lateness is printed as age in whole days rather than a made-up overdue flag. Seats remain workflow declarations, not authentication. No blocker.

**New gap discovered (Step 3), added to Planned below:** **matrix line sunset and two-sided re-affirmation — the term of office a declared line was never given** [frontline / mid-manager / director × matrix] — ADR-0148 records an INITIAL answer and ADR-0152 settles what a line leaves behind when it ends, but nothing gives a declared line a **term**: a project line declared "until further notice" that has run three years has never been re-affirmed by either manager or the person, and its allocation is inherited forever because no act ever revisited it. Would read each declared line's declared term (or its absence) against a printed convention, flag `no-term-declared` / `reaffirmation-due` / `reaffirmation-overdue` as structural findings on the LINE (never a person rating), and require a dated, two-sided reconfirmation by the managers and the person on the CURRENT share before the line can continue past its term — refusing to renew silently, and never reusing the original consent (40% accepted two years ago is not consent to 40% today). Draws on sunset-clause governance (Madisonian sunset provisions), Goold & Campbell's matrix design criteria (clarity of duration as a design variable) and the permanent-versus-temporary matrix literature (Hardy 1994); targeted search found no line-term or re-affirmation model in the repository.
