## 2026-11-09 — Two managers agreed on what Sam did, but not on what good looked like: Cross-Line Assessment Reconciliation & Calibration Parity (Session 209, Schema v126, [ADR-0151](./docs/adr/0151-cross-line-assessment-reconciliation.md), CSV #113, `#/reviews?panel=stewardship` Reconciliation)

**Implemented — director / VP PRIMARY × matrix; every altitude reads the same ledger; single-chain fully supported.** The real duty: a director runs calibration with Dana and Priya, both of whom had Sam for nine months. Both were asked. Both answered. Their packets sit side by side — one says "own the migration, mentor Kim, change the on-call policy", the other says "missed two milestones and needed daily support". The packet printed the words. Nothing in the workspace said whether those accounts **agree** — whether one line's coarse judgement diverges from the other's by two steps on the shared scale, whether one line wrote a sentence while another wrote a paragraph, or whether the comparison is even valid because a line never spoke. A thin "looks good" was silently treated as agreement with a detailed assessment. Session 203 closed whether every line **spoke**; this closes what they **said**, and whether calibration can trust it.

**Built.** One bounded read model (`assessmentReconciliation.js`) over the **existing** stewardship data, plus one optional first-person signal on each answer. Stored: `stewardship.answers[].signal` — one coarse human mark per line on a closed four-step scale (`needs-support` 0 → `as-expected` 1 → `strong` 2 → `exceptional` 3), declared only by the manager who holds the line inside their own answer. Derived on every read and never stored: every signal gap, every thin flag, every verdict and every total. Seven verdicts with declared precedence (`incomplete` → `single-answer` → `unrated-pair` → `thin-input` → `divergent` → `aligned` → `single-chain`), so the board, the packet card and the CSV cannot disagree. Four clamped conventions (thin character floor 20–500/120, thin ratio 2–20/3, divergent steps 1–3/2, board cap 40) — printed on the Method panel, on the Packet card and in the export, never fitted.

**The refusals that are the product.** (1) **No inference from prose** — two paragraphs are never auto-compared for sentiment; divergence is ONLY exact integer arithmetic over declared signals, so a paragraph with no signal makes the packet `unrated-pair` with the blank lines named, never silently mapped to a neighbour. (2) An `unasked` or `overdue` line makes the whole reconciliation `incomplete`, never silently excluded. (3) No score and no ranking — `divergent` is a prompt for calibration, never a rating. (4) A line that declined is never given a zero signal and never counted as agreement. (5) `thin-input` flags a sentence beside a paragraph as "check this", never "this is worse" — the thin threshold is character length, not substance, and both figures are printed. (6) The assessor line is not "another input" and is excluded from the count. (7) A single-line person is inert: no row, no ask, no verdict.

Next rotation: **frontline / mid-manager × matrix**, with the matrix read-model parity audit still In Progress.

## 2026-11-09 — Every line that onboarded this person, or never did: Matrix Onboarding Completeness (Session 208, Schema v125, [ADR-0150](./docs/adr/0150-matrix-onboarding-completeness.md), `RULE-ONB-01`, CSV #112, `#/onboarding?panel=matrix`)

**Implemented — frontline / mid-manager PRIMARY × matrix; every altitude reads the same ledger; single-chain fully supported.** The real duty: Sam joins on Monday with Dana as her functional manager and Priya holding 40% of her for a project. The 30-60-90 plan names role clarity, a buddy, the stakeholders, an early win and three check-ins — all written by one line about one job. Nothing recorded that Priya's line had any onboarding obligation at all, so a project manager never said in writing what Sam owes that project and Sam was never told; the plan read as the whole story, and a *completed* plan read as a completed onboarding of a person with two managers. Session 207's discovery named exactly this gap; the audit found `onboarding.js` carrying zero matrix references.

**Built.** One bounded read model (`onboardingMatrix.js`), three dated commands plus a reasoned refusal for each and an explicit scan (`onboardingMatrixActions.js`), and one rule on the shared spine. Stored: a NEW collection `onboardingLineBriefs` — one dated human statement per row (plan, person, line, manager, scope, first work, stakeholders, or an explicit decline with a reason) plus the person's own dated acknowledgement of **that exact text** — and `onboardingLineBriefMarkers` for the rule. Derived on every read and never stored: every line state, every window, every overdue count in whole days, the duplicate-plan finding, the presumption and every total.

**The refusals that are the product.** (1) **Two claims, two figures** — `crossLineComplete` (every line wrote and the person acknowledged) and the plan's own `status === 'completed'` are printed side by side and never merged; a line that declined reads `crossLineSettled`, a weaker word, never `complete`. (2) A line that wrote nothing reads `unbriefed` or `awaiting-brief`, never a zero. (3) **One person, one case** — two concurrent plans are one case with the duplicate named, and `peopleN` is a set of distinct people, never plan-line pairs. (4) The home line with no brief reads `presumed`, printed as a presumption and never counted as a settled line. (5) A brief is written only by the seat that holds the line; an acknowledgement only by the person — a manager acknowledging for a report is refused with that reason. (6) A decline needs a stated reason. (7) An acknowledged brief cannot be overwritten in place; a re-brief is a NEW row that re-asks the person (and same-day rows are ordered by the order the store recorded them, the only truthful tie-break). (8) No plan is invented for a multi-line person who has none.

Next rotation: **director / VP × matrix**, with the matrix read-model parity audit still In Progress (the as-of matrix read remains blocked on the historical home graph).

## 2026-11-09 — The org chart gets a history: Matrix Reorganisation Reconciliation & As-Of Structure Reads (Session 206, Schema v124, [ADR-0149](./docs/adr/0149-matrix-reorganisation-reconciliation.md), `RULE-SHR-01`, CSV #111, `#/structure-history`)

**Implemented — director / VP PRIMARY × matrix; every altitude reads the same ledger; single-chain fully supported.** The real duty: the week after eleven people move between teams, a VP asks *what did the structure look like on the day this acceptance was written* — and the product, which stores `person.managerId` as a pointer with no history, answers with today. Every stored act naming a manager was silently re-read against the present. This is the gap Sessions 203, 204 and 205 each named and none could close.

**Built.** One bounded read model (`structureHistory.js`), three dated commands (`structureRecordMove`, `structureSeedCurrent`, `structureImportDesign`) plus an explicit scan, and one rule on the shared spine. Stored: `structureHistory` — one row per **observed home-line period** (person, manager, valid-time `fromISO`/`toISO`, **transaction-time `recordedOn`**, recording seat, source, reason) — plus `structureHistoryMarkers`. Derived on every read and never stored: every observation state, every span, every joined/left/held verdict, every uncomparable count, every act reading. Three observation states (`observed`, `unknown`, `not-on-roster`), four verdicts (`observed`, `partial`, `unrecorded`, `future`) and four act states (`consistent`, `drifted`, `unverifiable`, `undated`), each with declared precedence.

**The refusals that are the product.** (1) A day the ledger does not cover is `unknown` and **every derived figure is withheld** — never today's roster projected backwards; a workspace upgraded to v124 has no recorded past and says exactly that. (2) A partial reading withholds the spans rather than printing a smaller, tidy list over the people it happens to cover, naming the fraction. (3) **Drift is reported, never corrected** — nothing is re-pointed, migrated or withdrawn; `RULE-SHR-01` asks the manager who holds the line *now*, and a human decides. (4) `unverifiable` is not `consistent`: an act in an unrecorded window is neither confirmed nor contradicted. (5) `appeared`, `disappeared` and `moved` are three counts, because a joiner is not a mover. (6) The pointer and the ledger move in **one transaction**. (7) `structureSeedCurrent` records today and claims nothing about yesterday — explicitly not a back-fill.

## 2026-11-09 — A declared share is an ask until two people answer it: Matrix Line Consent (Session 204, Schema v123, [ADR-0148](./docs/adr/0148-matrix-line-consent.md), `RULE-LCN-01`, CSV #110, `#/matrix?panel=consent`)

**Implemented — frontline / mid-manager PRIMARY × matrix.** The real duty: a project manager has been given 40% of an engineer she has never agreed a delivery with, and nobody has told the engineer. The matrix ledger printed that 40% as though it were agreed, and every roll-up inherited it. Shadow accountability was the one failure the register itself created: it recorded a *declaration* and had no way to record an *answer*.

**Built.** One bounded read model (`lineConsent.js`), two first-person commands plus a reasoned refusal and an explicit scan (`lineConsentActions.js`), and one rule on the shared spine. Stored: `lineConsents` — one dated act per row, with the side that answered, the outcome, the seat, the window an acceptance runs to, the **share that was accepted**, an optional basis and a mandatory decline reason; plus `lineConsentMarkers`. Derived on every read and never stored: every line state, every lapse, every day count, every person verdict and every total. Six line states (`unanswered`, `declined`, `changed`, `lapsed`, `awaiting-person`, `accepted`) and seven verdicts with declared precedence. New rights `accept-matrix-line` and `acknowledge-matrix-line` on the seat spine — registered, because an unregistered right refuses every seat including the operator.

**The refusals that are the product.** (1) A declaration is not an acceptance: `unanswered` is its own word, and *declared* and *accepted* are printed as two different figures. (2) A refusal is an answer, not a deletion: a declined line stays charged and the count of those is printed. (3) **A retuned share is not a consented share** — the acceptance stores the number it was given for, so a retune from 40% to 90% reads `changed`, prints both numbers, excludes itself from the accepted total, and re-asks at the new share. (4) An acceptance that would commit more than 100% of a person is refused with the arithmetic printed; when any share is undeclared the capacity check is *refused*, not guessed. (5) If any line in scope has no allocation, both share totals are refused with the reason — never a total over a part. (6) Only the line's manager may accept or decline and only the person may acknowledge; where the person has no seat, the operator may capture the statement and the row is marked `operator`, never printed as authentication.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **frontline / mid-manager primary 204** (previous primary 203); director / VP 197; CEO / C-suite 198. **Structure: single-chain 1–188; MATRIX primary 189–198, 200, 203 and 204.** Single-chain unchanged: no row, no marker, no ask, no edge. Next rotation: **director / VP × matrix**, with the matrix read-model parity audit still In Progress.

**Verified (one focused pass).** `tests/app/matrix-line-consent.test.mjs` — **18/18 PASS**: a declared share nobody answered reads `unanswered` and nothing is inferred; an undeclared allocation refuses both totals and still counts states; the home manager and a peer are refused when accepting; accept → acknowledge round-trips through the real storage adapter and survives reload with display == stored; the person cannot acknowledge before acceptance and cannot acknowledge twice; a manager cannot acknowledge on the person's behalf; a decline needs a reason, is stored, and the share stays charged; accepting past one whole person is refused with `110%` in the message; a lapsed acceptance reads lapsed and can be re-accepted; a retune reads `changed` with both numbers printed and a re-ask at the new share; `RULE-LCN-01` issues exactly one ask per line idempotently and addresses the acknowledgement ask to the PERSON; rule/contract spine 1:1; schema v123 additive and clamps its three conventions; an acceptance with no expiry is dropped at load; a single-chain workspace is inert end to end; the CSV scope is aggregate-only and its counts equal the computed report; and a JSDOM render prints the stored state, the stored share and the stored window. Adjacent suites re-run green: `core` **15/15**, `csv` **5/5**, `matrix-accountability` + `review-stewardship` **41/41**, `access-audit` (in the boundary pass). `npm run lint` PASS; `npm run check:boundary` PASS (622 app ES modules, 196 test suites, 23 doc checks, 0 leaks); `npm run check:links` PASS (986 links across 265 files).

## 2026-11-09 — Every line that assessed this person, or never spoke: Matrix Multi-Line Review Stewardship (Session 203, Schema v122, [ADR-0147](./docs/adr/0147-matrix-review-stewardship.md), `RULE-SRV-01`, CSV #109, `#/reviews?panel=stewardship`)

**Implemented — frontline / mid-manager PRIMARY × matrix.** The real duty: the review period just closed, and the person who writes the assessment is one of two managers the person delivered for. The packet assembled itself from `personId` alone, so a project line's evidence sat in it while nobody asked that line what it saw, a line could contribute nothing and the packet still read as a complete account of the period, and a contested `performance` right was silently resolved to whichever line wrote first. Those are three different failures, and each one now has its own name instead of one reassuring word.

**Built.** One bounded read model (`reviewStewardship.js`) and three dated, span-checked commands. Stored on the review row so it freezes with the packet: the asks (`stewardship.requests`) and the line holders' own first-person answers, or a decline with a stated reason (`stewardship.answers`). Derived on every read and never stored: every period line, every line state, every overdue flag with whole overdue days, the assessor resolution, the verdict and every total. Six line states (`assessor`, `answered`, `declined`, `asked`, `overdue`, `unasked`, plus `excluded` for a line outside the period) and seven verdicts with declared precedence, so the rule, the panel and the CSV cannot disagree about a word. `RULE-SRV-01` runs immediately before the Operating Seat and issues at most one owned, dated delegation per unasked line, addressed to the manager who holds it — and issues NOTHING when the assessor is contested or undeclared, because a task addressed to nobody could never close. Three panels (`board`, `packet`, `method`), seven route aliases under `#/reviews`, CSV scope #109, and three declared API rights (`ask-review-input`, `answer-review-input`, plus the safe aggregate reads).

**The refusal that is the product.** No per-line contribution share is computed or printed. Feedback, recognition, 1:1 notes and delegations record who an item is ABOUT, never which line produced it, so any split would be a fabricated allocation every downstream figure inherits. The report carries `lineAttributable: false` with the reason, printed on the panel and on every CSV row. The project manager's missing evidence reads as a named process gap — not as a zero contribution, and not as an invented share.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **frontline / mid-manager primary 203** (previous primary 200); director / VP 197; CEO / C-suite 198. **Structure: single-chain 1–188; MATRIX primary 189–198, 200 and 203.** Single-chain unchanged: no row, no warning, no edge, no delegation. ## 2026-11-09 — Repeated matrix friction becomes a structural signal (Session 198, Schema v121 unchanged, [ADR-0146](./docs/adr/0146-matrix-recurring-structural-patterns.md), CSV #108, `#/matrix?panel=concordance`)

**Implemented — CEO / C-suite PRIMARY × matrix; the same seat-scoped read is available to every altitude.** Single-chain workspaces remain inert. The chief's duty: distinguish a one-off exception from a repeated pattern in how the matrix's decision rights work, without turning repeated friction into a score on the people involved.

**New gap discovered by proactive discovery and entered into Planned before implementation:** the workspace could audit each decision but could not aggregate the same structural finding across distinct decisions. A targeted inspection confirmed `rightsConcordance.js` emitted per-decision findings only; no recurring-pattern lens existed. The gap was real; the bounded read model was built in this session.

**What shipped.** An identity-free recurrence model groups findings by structural kind + active line-kind set + affected rights, counts distinct decisions (one decision contributes at most once to a pattern even when several linked subjects share it), marks a pattern recurring only at two or more decisions, and shows first/latest dates. Its 12-row queue counts its remainder. The matrix Concordance panel, matrix brief and existing aggregate CSV scope #108 all consume the same computed report. No names, person/manager/line/decision/case ids, titles or rationale enter recurrence rows or recurrence CSV data.

**Shared system.** Reuses ADR-0145's typed provenance graph, the date-specific canonical `buildMatrix`, and the matrix report's `matrixLineScopeFor` / seat scope. It adds no second hierarchy, event engine or stored derived values. This is a pure read: a repeated pattern prompts human design review and cannot change a line or open work on its own.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **CEO / C-suite primary 198** (last 195); director / VP 197; frontline / mid-manager 196. **Structure: single-chain 1–188; MATRIX primary 189–198.** Next primary rotation: frontline / mid-manager × matrix; the matrix read-model parity audit remains **In Progress**.

## 2026-11-09 — The decision log is now audited against the rights the lines declared: the Matrix Decision-Right Execution Concordance (Session 197, Schema v121 unchanged, [ADR-0145](./docs/adr/0145-rights-concordance.md), CSV #108, `#/matrix?panel=concordance`)

**Implemented — director / VP PRIMARY × matrix; every altitude reading the matrix report inherits it; a single-chain workspace is inert.** The duty: a director or VP who has just read the matrix's declared rights and the contradiction audit's charters asks the dated reverse about the DECISION LOG — "we recorded that this manager decided this, on this day; did the structure we declared actually give them the authority, and were the people the structure says must be heard recorded as heard?" Session 196's roadmap named this exact gap as its next discovery, flagged `[UNVERIFIED]` pending a full repository audit; the audit found it real.

**The measured gap.** A targeted search found no reader joining the decision log to the declared rights: `decisions` carry DACI names and `decidedOn` dates, the typed provenance graph links decisions to people and cases, the matrix ledger declares per-line windows and six RAPID rights — and nothing compared the two. A declared right no decision ever respects is decoration; a decision made by a manager the structure gave no right to is a bypass that will be re-fought every time, because the next ruling has no precedent to point at.

**What shipped.** A pure read model, `app/core/domain/rightsConcordance.js` + `rightsConcordanceRegistry.js`, wired into the existing `buildMatrixReport` as an eighth panel (`concordance`), the matrix brief, and a new CSV scope #108. **No new collection, node, relation, rule, event, action, setting or schema bump** — `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 121; everything is re-derived on every render from records the workspace already writes.

- **The join, per completed decision.** The subject — whose lines' rights govern — resolves ONLY through typed provenance edges the workspace already writes (a link to a person, or to a case whose recorded owner is the person). A decision with no such edge is counted **unscoped and printed, never guessed** into the approver's span. The subject's active lines are re-derived by the real `buildMatrix` AT THE DECISION DATE, so a line declared after the decision, or ended before it, is excluded by the same engine the rest of the workspace uses.
- **Four structural findings, each about a decision against the declared structure, never a person rating.** `bypass` (the recorded decider held no declared right on any active line), `contested-decided` (the decider held a right two or more managers hold — the duplicate-approval risk), `unresolved-authority` (a right held by nobody on the decision date — the decision filled the gap), `consult-gap` (an operational-right holder — priority, assignment, technical — not recorded among the contributors; stewardship holders are not required to be consulted on a work decision, and the convention is printed so it can be argued with). The panel says where a reader would look for a rating that the module refuses to produce.
- **Four scope limits, counted and never mapped into a finding.** `unresolved-decider` (a decider name that does not resolve to the roster — DACI names are free text by design, a decision may be made with someone outside it — or resolves ambiguously to two people), `single-line-subject` (the matrix module's own scope is people on MORE than one line; these decisions are counted and audited nothing), `unscoped-decision`, `dangling-subject`. Every count the panel prints is one of the identities asserted in the suite: `audited = withFindings + clean`, `findings = shown + withheld`, `queue = shown + remainder`, `completed = audited + unscoped + singleLine`.
- **Seat-scoped exactly as the matrix report.** The concordance runs inside `buildMatrixReport`, which injects the acting seat and its scope; findings whose subject sits outside the seat's span are counted `withheld` and never shown — the audit widens a seat to its own people, never sideways. Nothing is written: the state is byte-identical after a read, pinned by test.

**A pre-existing shipped defect found by driving the live API, fixed in place.** The matrix module gates every one of its commands — reads included — on the declared right `declare-matrix-line`, but that right was never registered in `ACTION_RIGHTS`, the seat spine's single source of truth. The live API therefore refused `matrixReport`, `matrixBriefText`, `matrixCsvRows` and `matrixCandidates` for EVERY seat, including the undeclared operator view: the whole matrix terminal was unreachable through the shipped application, not just for seats a test happened to exercise. The right is now registered (rank 1–5, every leadership seat, the same window as `declare-line-mandate`), with the comment recording why an unregistered right fails closed for everybody.

**Shared engine / roll-up wiring.** Reuses `buildMatrix` at each decision date (the per-date matrix cache), `linksForEntity` for subjects, `matrixLineScopeFor`/`buildSeats` for the seat scope, the decision-log grammar (`splitParticipants`), and the matrix report's own seat injection. No new hierarchy, no second window implementation, no new graph edge.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **director / VP primary 197** (previous primary 193); CEO / C-suite 195; frontline / mid-manager 196. **Structure: single-chain 1–188; MATRIX primary 189–197.** Next rotation: CEO / C-suite × matrix again, with the ~60-module matrix read-model audit still **In Progress**.

**Verification (one focused pass):** new `rights-concordance` suite **27/27 PASS** (`node --test`), covering the four identities on a mixed workspace, subject resolution through both typed routes, the unscoped / dangling / ambiguous / unresolved-decider limits, the single-line scope boundary, date-windowed line rights (declared-after, ended-before, presumed home rights), all four findings with their exact negative cases, seat withholding and the full-access seat, the byte-identical no-write check, CSV round-trip equality with no person, name or id in any cell, the inert single-chain workspace, the axe-clean JSDOM panel render, panel registration, and the store-backed API carrying the concordance. The build pass caught two real defects: the CSV export indexed kebab-case finding keys against camelCase accumulators (three of the four kinds printed 0 — mapping now declared once, with the comment recording that the export must never print a zero for a kind that fired), and the missing `declare-matrix-line` registration above. Full canonical suite, standalone build and real-browser AT walkthrough **[UNVERIFIED]** — the focused pass is the verification; no blocker.

**New gap discovered (Step 3), added to Planned:** **matrix line acceptance** is already planned below; this session's own honest next-target is the matrix read-model parity sweep itself — the ~60 modules that still reason over a tree, of which the concordance's build-time audit found one more instance (the matrix actions' right registration) and which cannot be closed module-by-module without a per-module audit of what a seat's scope SHOULD contain. ## 2026-11-09 — Two charters that cannot both hold: the Cross-Line Contradiction Audit (Session 195, Schema v121, [ADR-0144](./docs/adr/0144-cross-line-contradiction-audit.md), `RULE-CNT-01`, CSV #107, `#/contradiction`)

**Implemented — CEO / C-suite PRIMARY × matrix; director and VP rule within their span, mid-manager and frontline declare and read, and a single-chain workspace is untouched.** The real duty: the chief planning next quarter, who has just arbitrated a precedence for one engineer and can see it will be re-fought next quarter unless the *charters* that produced it are audited. Session 194 built the adjudication. This builds the reverse direction: not "which demand goes first" but "do two lines' declared objectives, incentives or envelope claims make one another permanently unachievable for the people on both?"

**The measured gap.** `grep` over `app/core/domain/` found no lever, direction, incentive weight or coupling model anywhere: goals carry a title and a key result, budgets carry a ceiling, and neither says *which operating lever this line is paid to move, in which direction*. Session 194's own next-target list named this item, and it is the only remaining item that reads the design rather than an instance of it.

**What was built.** Two stored collections (`lineMandates`, `contradictionReviews`) plus `contradictionMarkers`, four printed conventions, `RULE-CNT-01` on the shared post-commit spine (registered immediately before `seatRule`), a four-panel terminal at `#/contradiction` with seven route aliases and a badge, CSV scope #107, three rights (`declare-line-mandate`, `review-contradiction`, `set-contradiction-conventions`) and five safe reads.

- **A closed lever taxonomy, because a metric name is not comparable.** Ten levers (throughput, lead time, utilisation, inventory, service level, cost, quality, growth, margin, risk) with declared units. A lever outside the taxonomy is refused at the normalizer, never mapped to a neighbour.
- **Only one coupling is provable, and it says so.** Utilisation against lead time carries Kingman's VUT arithmetic — τ/(100−τ) at the declared target, printed beside the declared knee — and reads `incompatible` only above it. Inventory/service, cost/quality, growth/margin, throughput/quality and utilisation/quality are named as **trade-offs**, because a deliberate process change moves those frontiers and claiming impossibility would be false.
- **Severity is four words, not one.** `incompatible` (shown from declared integers or the queueing law), `tension` (declared trade-off), `isolated` (no person on both lines — counted, never counted as a contradiction), `insufficient` (a figure was not declared, named).
- **Incentives are summed exactly.** A person's scorecard is the sum of the charters of every line they sit on, in integer basis points: above 10000 at least one payout is unachievable by construction, and an opposite-direction pair above the declared materiality floor is a Kerr problem in the scorecard, not in the person.
- **Envelope claims are measured against the envelope's own recorded ceiling.** Three claimants that together claim 130% is exact arithmetic against a stored limit; a claim on a closed or deleted envelope is refused and printed, never counted.
- **Two acts, never one.** `contradictionReview` records accepted / resequenced / withheld. RULE-CNT-01 opens exactly one governed decision per ruling and issues dated work **only** for a resequence, **only** to the named line. Idempotent through a per-review and a per-review-per-line marker.

**Engine defects found by the first run and fixed in place.** The new conventions were silently dropped on every load because `normalizeSettings` rebuilds settings field by field — the spread into `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` was not enough, so the printed knee would have been a number the record did not hold. The finding-key grammar rejected the engine's own `~` separator, so a valid ruling could never reload. The duplicate-charter guard compared `effectiveFrom === null` against a row that always carries a date, so a second identical charter could double a share. The envelope finding's shared-person count looked only at the first two claimants, so a three-way claim could report catching nobody. And the CSV exported the board's forty-row render slice rather than every finding, which is precisely the silent drop the mandate forbids.

**Shared engine / roll-up wiring.** Reuses `buildMatrix`/`matrixLineScope`, `buildSeats`/`activeSeat`/`canAct`, the typed-link graph (`concerns`, `decides`, `issues-obligation`, `rolls-up-to` — no new relation), `ensureEntityLink`, the post-commit spine and the governed-decision path. `RULE-CNT-01` is in `PROPAGATION_CONTRACTS`; the spine parity pin moved 92 → 93 deliberately.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **CEO / C-suite primary 195** (last primary 191); director / VP last primary 193; frontline / mid-manager last primary 194. **Structure: single-chain 1–188, MATRIX primary 189–195.** Next rotation: frontline / mid-manager × matrix, with the ~60-module matrix read-model audit still **In Progress**; then matrix line acceptance.

**Verification (one focused pass):** new `contradiction-audit` suite **21/21 PASS**, including the queueing multiplier against an independent rational oracle, severity honesty at and below the knee, the missing-target refusal, isolated-vs-incompatible, exact 12000 bp oversubscription, the materiality floor, the exact envelope over-claim, nine action refusals, one-decision-plus-one-obligation-on-resequence with idempotent rescan, acceptance issuing no work, spine/contract/entity-type parity, CSV round-trip equality with no person, line id or reasoning in any cell, and JSDOM + axe-core clean on all four panels. Adjacent suites re-run green: `core` 15/15, `csv` 5/5, `board-room` 45/45, `priority-arbitration` 22/22, `matrix-accountability` 24/24, `canonical-boundary` 7/7. `npm run lint` PASS (0 errors, 0 warnings); `check:boundary` PASS (607 modules / 190 suites / 23 doc checks); `check:links` PASS (966 links / 261 files). Stale pins corrected deliberately, not deleted: the migration chain in `core` and `board-room`, the CSV export count 105 → 106 in `csv` and `board-room`, the spine 92 → 93, and the v119/v120 head assertions in `matrix-accountability` and `priority-arbitration`.

**Unverified / flagged.** Full canonical suite (`npm test`) not run end to end; the suites above were run individually. Real-browser assistive-technology walkthrough [UNVERIFIED] (axe-core in jsdom is what ran). Cost / quality / growth / margin couplings are **declared**, not measured elasticities. The utilisation knee is a convention, not a measurement. A line's scorecard share is assumed to apply to every person on that line. Seats remain workflow declarations, not authentication. Blockers: none.

**New gap discovered (Step 3), added to Planned below:** **matrix transfer pricing and shared-service attribution** [director / VP / CEO × matrix] — when two lines draw on one platform, one data function or one shared service, the cost lands somewhere arbitrary and the audited envelope claims then measure a number nobody can defend. It would let a line declare consumption of a shared capacity, price it by a named method (activity-based costing or a Shapley split over declared usage), and print the residual that no method can attribute — so a line's P&L is comparable across a matrix instead of being a function of where the cost centre happens to sit. Distinct from ADR-0142's budget exposure (which reads an envelope once per seat) and from this audit (which measures claims against a ceiling): this prices *consumption of something shared*, and the honest output is the unattributable residual, never a fabricated allocation.

## 2026-11-08 — Which of two managers' dated work goes first: the Cross-Line Priority Arbitration (Session 194, Schema v120, [ADR-0143](./docs/adr/0143-cross-line-priority-arbitration.md), `RULE-ARB-01`, CSV #106, `#/arbitration`)

**Implemented — frontline / mid-manager PRIMARY × matrix; director, VP and CEO read the same case, and every altitude in a matrix inherits it.** The real duty: an engineer is 140% committed across two managers on paper, both managers have handed her dated work, and the only honest thing the old workspace could say was "priority is contested" — a true statement about the structure and a useless one at 09:00 on a Monday.

**The measured gap.** Session 193's discovered item named it: the ledger can expose a contested `priority` right and the declared capacity behind it, but it cannot turn that into one reviewed precedence agreement. `grep` found no arbitration, precedence, WSJF or cost-of-delay path anywhere in `app/core/domain/`. The contested-right finding was where the product stopped.

**What was built.** Two collections (`priorityArbitrations`, `priorityArbitrationMarkers`), three printed conventions, `RULE-ARB-01` on the shared post-commit spine (registered immediately before `seatRule`), typed links (`concerns`, `decides`, `rolls-up-to`, `issues-obligation`), CSV scope #106, a four-panel terminal, four findable route aliases and a nav badge. The case freezes each line's demand **as that line stated it**, with the two integers it declared; every figure is derived on read.

- **The rank is arguable.** WSJF as exact integer cross-multiplication (Reinertsen 2009 / the SAFe form), with critical-chain remaining days (Goldratt 1997) as an explicit multiplier. A missing cost of delay or job size is never scored 0: the case prints `incomplete`, names the demand that refused, and offers **no recommendation at all**.
- **A tie names the whole top group.** Two demands that measure identically are `contested` with the group size printed; row order never breaks a tie.
- **The arbiter is derived, or the ambiguity is printed.** `matrixJointApex` over the reporting DAG; a diamond tie stays a tie.
- **Two acts, never one.** `priorityPropose` records the measured order as a read model; `priorityAgreePrecedence` is the only command that issues work. The recommendation can be read and refused — it cannot act.
- **Dissent carries the same weight as agreement.** Each party answers as its own first-person act under **its own seat identity**; an agreement nobody answered is flagged `no-dissent-recorded`, never read as unanimity.
- **Capacity is measured against the declared ceiling** in whole hundredths; exceeding it reads `over-committed` with both numbers printed rather than blocking a plan humans are entitled to accept knowingly.

**Engine defects found by the first run and fixed in place.** Contest was computed from presumed home-line rights, which manufactured contention in every matrix; the tie group excluded the first row; allocation resolution assumed one shape (function/`Map`/array/list all accepted now, with a printed refusal when none is available); recorded answers were rewritten to `LEADER_ID`, fabricating leader consent and collapsing two parties into one record; and the verdict was validated against the wrong vocabulary, rejecting every real verdict.

**Shared engine / roll-up wiring.** Reuses `buildMatrix`/`matrixJointApex`, `buildSeats` with `matrixLineScopeFor`, the typed-link graph, `ensureEntityLink`, the post-commit spine and the governed-decision path. No isolated one-off: `RULE-ARB-01` is in `PROPAGATION_CONTRACTS`, pinned by the spine parity test at 92 rules.

**Altitude/structure coverage map:** **frontline / mid-manager primary 194** (last primary 187); director / VP last primary 193; CEO last primary 191. **Structure: single-chain 1–188, MATRIX primary 189–194.** Next rotation: CEO / C-suite × matrix, with the ~60-module matrix read-model audit still **In Progress**.

**Verification (one focused pass):** new `priority-arbitration` suite **22/22 PASS**, including exact integer rank vs. a cross-multiplication oracle, the incomplete-set refusal, the tie group, the diamond arbiter, per-party identity on answers, nothing issued before agreement and a governed decision plus dated obligations after it, idempotency on a second rule pass, CSV round-trip equality with the report, and JSDOM + axe-core clean across all four panels. Adjacent suites touched by the schema bump re-run and green (`board-room` 45/45, `csv` 5/5, `core`, `matrix-accountability` 24/24, `matrix-line-seat` 13/13, `matrix-governance` 7/7, `altitude-router` 16/16, `canonical-boundary` 7/7). `npm run lint`, `npm run check:boundary` (601 modules / 189 suites / 23 doc checks) and `npm run check:links` PASS. **Unverified / flagged.** Cost of delay and job size are declared integers, not measured money or effort; capacity is a declaration, not a calendar; the arbiter comes from declared reporting lines, not from authority actually exercised. Seats remain workflow declarations, not authentication. Blockers: none.

## 2026-11-08 — The work was fanned to a manager who had no seat to read it: matrix-safe ownership and scope (Session 190, Schema v119 unchanged, [ADR-0141](./docs/adr/0141-matrix-line-seat.md), `#/matrix?panel=seats` + `#/seat`)

**Implemented — director / VP PRIMARY; every altitude in a matrix inherits it, and a single-chain workspace is byte-identical.** The real duty: the product director who holds two engineers on declared project lines opens the workspace and must be able to answer "what is waiting on me, from the people my line carries". Session 189 gave the matrix its write side; this session gives it a read side.

**The measured gap.** ADR-0140 shipped `RULE-MTX-01`, which fans work touching a multi-line person to **every** manager in that person's reporting set — correct, and unchanged. The read path never learned about lines. Reproduced against the shipped code with an engineering director home-managing Sam and a product director holding Sam on a declared `project` line:

- `buildSeats` seats a node only when `span > 0 && altitude`; the tree gave the product director **no reports**, so she had **no operating seat at all**;
- declaring her as the active seat made `resolveSeat` fail closed to **read-only** ("that seat no longer exists") — the whole workspace locked, silently;
- `canSee` scoped the record to `seat.scope` (the tree subtree), so she was **denied** the goal of the person her own line carries, with the rank window permitting it;
- `seatDigest` counted only `seat.scope`, so even the denial was invisible: her span read **0 open items** while four existed;
- nothing anywhere counted the work a single-chain seat drops.

So the engine routed the work to a manager who could not be seated, could not be selected, and would have been refused the record. Two clauses of the Matrix Leadership Mandate — *never drop a person because their second line was invisible* and *never silently pick one of several managers as the owner* — were unimplemented on the read side.

**What was built.** `matrixLineScope(matrix)` derives the line-scope ONCE from `buildMatrix`'s already-active lines (primary excluded: the tree carries the home line) and returns, per manager, the people held, the line count, the kinds, and `lineOnlyIds` — the subset the tree hides from that manager. `matrixLineScopeFor(state, opts)` returns **`null`** when no line is declared, so the injected option is absent rather than empty and a single-chain workspace takes the pre-0141 path with no new keys on any seat (pinned by test). `buildSeats({ lineScope })` consumes it as **plain data** — `seat.js` imports nothing new and no import cycle exists between the seat engine and the matrix engine.

- **A seat for the second line, with no invented rung.** Eligibility becomes `(span > 0 || lineScopeN > 0) && altitude`. A line holder whose roster title carries **no** leadership altitude is **refused** a seat and printed (`refusedLineSeats` → Seats panel → identity-free brief); the rung is a fact about the roster, the line is a fact about the work, and the product manufactures neither.
- **Scope, not authority.** `canSee` admits a person reachable through the tree **or** an active declared line, and carries the route (`viaLine`, `lineScopedN`, `lineKinds`) so the screen can say which carried it. Rank windows, class floors and detail ceilings are untouched. One outsider in the record still **denies** it, and the refusal now names how many arrived by no route at all — the matrix widens a seat to its own line, never sideways.
- **The roll-up prints the split.** `seatDigest` adds `viaLineN` and `treeOpenN` with the exact identity `treeOpenN + viaLineN === openN`. The headline figure is the whole reading; the part a single-chain product would have hidden is printed beside it, never folded in.
- **Ownership named, never collapsed.** `matrixWorkReach` returns every accountable manager per open item — the tree owner plus every line manager who covers *all* named people — and `shared` is reported, not resolved. No single owner is emitted for work the structure gives more than one.
- **One resolution for the gate and the screen.** The API gate (`guardApiCall`), the seat read model (`seatRead`), the seat-declaration guard (`setActiveSeat`) and the disclosure export all hand the same lines to `buildSeats`, so nothing can display a seat the gate would refuse.
- **Reported where the leader acts**: `#/matrix?panel=seats` (line managers, tree span vs matrix span, only-via-line counts, refusals with reasons, and a printed reconciliation), `#/seat` (the same two count fields), five additive CSV columns (`line_scope_n`, `line_only_n`, `line_work_n`, `line_work_shared_n`, `seat_state`) on the existing `matrix` scope with a `seat` row kind, and one clause in the identity-free brief.

**Altitude coverage map (Session 190):** frontline last primary 187; mid-manager last primary 187; **director / VP primary 190**; CEO / C-suite last primary 188. **Structure coverage: single-chain 1–188, MATRIX primary 189 and 190 — the read path is now matrix-safe.** Next rotation: **CEO / C-suite**, with the matrix structure remaining the standing second axis.

## 2026-11-08 — A person on four lines is 140% committed, and every roll-up said 100%: the Matrix Accountability Ledger (Session 189, Schema v119, [ADR-0140](./docs/adr/0140-matrix-accountability-ledger.md), `#/matrix`)

**Implemented — director / VP PRIMARY; frontline, mid-manager and CEO read the same reconciliation, and every altitude in a matrix inherits it.** The real duty: the engineering director who has just been asked "can Sam take the migration as well?" and the project manager asking the same question in the next meeting, each believing — correctly, from where they sit — that Sam is theirs. Neither can see the other's ask, and no dashboard in the product could add them up.

**The measured gap.** The hierarchy is `person.managerId`, a single pointer. `buildChain` reads it into a tree, and every roll-up in the workspace is a property of that tree — ownership by lowest common ancestor, span of control, the seat's disclosure ladder, `RULE-SEAT-01`'s fan-out, the Jaques altitude clock. A tree's answer is unique *because a tree has exactly one path to the root*; add a second line and the same question has two defensible answers. `grep -i matrix` over `app/core/domain/` before this session returned only linear algebra (Cholesky, design matrices), 2×2 grids (Mendelow) and the Hoshin X-Matrix: **no structural matrix support anywhere.** Session 188's coverage map named director/VP as the next hierarchy rotation, and the Universal Matrix Hierarchy Mandate gives an entirely-neglected *structure* default priority over another rung of a structure the product already serves.

**What was built.** `reportingLines` (Schema v119) stores only the human act — this person is also accountable to that manager, on this kind of line, for this many **whole hundredths** of their capacity, holding these decision rights, from this day until that day. `buildMatrix` wraps `buildChain` and ADDS the declared lines on top; the home line is never copied, so a workspace that declares nothing gains no edges, no decisions and no behaviour change (pinned by test). On top of it:

- **The reconciliation.** Two separate claims, never one word. `balances` — the allocations add up to the headcount. `auditClean` — the printed total is exactly the sum of the printed rows, and the manager fan-out equals the person total. An earlier draft exposed one flag called `reconciles`, which let a reader hear "it adds up" from a ledger whose net error was `+0.30`; the split is the fix. All arithmetic is **integer hundredths**, so the reconciliation is exact rather than something that rounds into looking correct.
- **Attribution is all-or-nothing.** One line owns the whole person, by arithmetic, labelled `sole-line`. Two lines with a hole in them own **nothing to anybody** — filling the hole evenly would be an agreement nobody made. This was a real bug the suite caught: the person total was refused while the manager span still credited the lines that happened to carry a number.
- **Decision rights (RAPID, Rogers & Blenko 2006).** Six rights attributed per line. Two managers holding one is `contested`; nobody holding it is `unowned`. The register records both and adjudicates neither — both are properties of the structure, not of a person. The home line is *presumed* to hold pay, performance and absence, printed as a presumption on every row it touches, and outvoted into a contest the moment any line declares one.
- **`RULE-MTX-01`** fans work to **every** manager in a person's reporting set, registered immediately before `seatRule` so one atomic commit carries both fans. It never picks which of two managers *owns* an item — that is a decision the engine is not entitled to make. Inert in a single-chain workspace; a confidential source contributes a count and never an edge.
- Refusals, not repairs: a self-line, a duplicate home declaration, an unparseable allocation and a line that would close a loop are each named on the Review panel. A semantically impossible row is **kept in storage** rather than silently deleted at load.

**Altitude coverage map (Session 189):** frontline last primary 187; mid-manager last primary 187; **director / VP primary 189**; CEO / C-suite last primary 188. **Structure coverage: single-chain 1–188, MATRIX primary 189 — first session to serve it at all.** Next rotation: CEO / C-suite, and the matrix structure is now the standing second axis of the map.

**Verified (one focused pass).** New `matrix-accountability` suite **23/23**: both identities as exact integer equalities including the case where the audit is clean and the ledger still does not balance; undeclared-share attribution refused rather than split; sole-line derivation labelled; netting refused (Sam +40 / Kim −40 still reports both); loop, self-line, duplicate and unparseable-share refusals; contested and unowned rights; the home-line presumption and its outvoting; `RULE-MTX-01` fanning to every manager and writing nothing in a single-chain workspace; the rule registered on the spine *and* in `PROPAGATION_CONTRACTS`; and **the display-vs-stored check** — the CSV's `attributed_h` / `net_fte_error_h` equal the report's computed values, no export row names a person, and the brief cannot say "reconciles exactly" when the net error is non-zero. Adjacent suites across everything touched (schema, store, CSV, command chain, operating seat, propagation ledger, cases automation, workspace navigation, typed links, disclosure compiler, export disclosure) **142/145 — the 3 failures re-confirmed PRE-EXISTING on a clean worktree of the base commit** (`schema v82 is additive`, `savepoint: copy-on-write`, `collapse: the whole real chain`). `npm run check:boundary` PASS (595 modules / 186 suites / 23 doc checks, 0 leaks); `npm run check:links` PASS. Full canonical suite, standalone build and real-browser AT walkthrough **[UNVERIFIED]**.

**Unverified / flagged.** An allocation is a declaration, not a measurement — nothing checks it against a calendar, and the panel says so. The 118 → 119 bump moved 119 test files' schema pins; the sweep was textual and the affected suites were re-run, but a pin in a suite outside the focused set could still have been missed. `balanceHundredths` (5) and `expiringDays` (14) are declared conventions, not measured optima. Seats remain workflow declarations, not authentication. Blockers: none.

**Next targets.** [CEO / C-suite] next hierarchy rotation; [matrix, all altitudes] **attribution integrity** (below); [matrix, all altitudes] a matrix-safe `responsibleNodeId`; [all altitudes] authenticated identity + tenant boundary (standing foundational item).

## 2026-11-08 — A span holding one assessed pair is not a rate: the board roll-up applies the cell floor it declares (Session 188, Schema v118 unchanged, [ADR-0139](./docs/adr/0139-board-partition-cell-floor.md), `#/board?panel=rollup`)

**Implemented — CEO / C-suite PRIMARY; director, VP and every altitude reading a board memo inherit the same suppressed surface.** The real duty: the chief standing in front of the board, asked "and how does that break down by team?" The roll-up panel is the answer to that question, and an answer that names a director with a 100% reading built on one assessed pair is worse than no answer.

**The measured gap.** `boardEvaluateClaim` has withheld a claim's rate below `boardCellFloor` (default 5) since ADR-0085. `boardPartition` — the reader that decomposes that same claim over the reporting tree — never applied it. Reproduced against the shipped code: a claim carrying 6 observations, partitioned over three spans, printed `Sam Director: 1 observation, 1 passing, 100% (interval 20.7–100)`. The same defect ADR-0091 fixed in `moduleAggregate`, one layer down. It was worse than a missing floor: the claim's own pass count is published at claim level by the evaluator, the memo text and the CSV, so withholding exactly one cell does not protect it — the reader subtracts the printed cells and the withheld cell is determined.

**What was built.** `boardSuppression.suppressPartitionRows` models the published surface as it is actually read (a cell prints its pass and fail counts; the claim's published pass count is the table's total) and runs the SAME ADR-0091 procedure the rest of the app uses — sub-floor cells withheld, then a partner cell hidden cheapest-first until no withheld cell is pinned, and **refusal** when the boxes saturate. `boardPartition` returns only the published surface, so `boardRules.worstOwner` can no longer pick an owner from a cell the board was never shown: a failing claim with a fully withheld decomposition opens the governed decision and delegates no obligation, recording why. A withheld cell keeps its identity and loses its figure; observation counts are still printed and still reconcile. Suppression travels as `cells_total` / `cells_withheld` / `partition_state` / `partition_floor` on the existing `board-claims` CSV scope — counts and words, never a cell label or figure. A declared floor of 1 is honoured as "publish everything". Also fixed the shared `table()` component emitting an empty `<th>` for action columns (`empty-table-header`), which every table in the app inherited.

**Altitude coverage map (Session 188):** frontline last primary 187; mid-manager last primary 187; director last primary 186; VP last primary 186; **CEO / C-suite primary 188**. Next rotation: **director / VP**.

**Verified (one focused pass).** New `board-partition-suppression` suite **9/9**: the exact regression string is gone, all-sub-floor cells withheld with counts reconciling, complementary suppression proven by counting the reader's own remainder, the floor-of-1 setting honoured, no obligation delegated off a withheld decomposition, the CSV carrying suppression without a cell label, and the roll-up panel axe-clean with cells withheld. Adjacent `board-continuity` + `board-room` + `aggregate-determinacy` + `csv` **77/77**. `npm run lint` PASS; `npm run check:boundary` PASS (589 modules / 185 suites / 23 doc checks, 0 leaks); `npm run check:links` PASS. Full canonical suite, standalone build and real-browser AT walkthrough **[UNVERIFIED]**.

**Unverified / flagged.** A withheld cell's OBSERVATION count remains derivable from the published claim denominator — the withholding's own reason announces as much — so what is protected is the RATING, and the panel prints that limit. Suppression is small-cell withholding, not differential privacy. A REFUSED decomposition is not a claim-level refusal: the verdict still stands on the claim's full denominator. Seats remain workflow declarations, not authentication.

## 2026-11-08 — One writer for the 1:1 queue: their own topics can no longer be deleted by an engine cascade (Session 187, Schema v118 unchanged, [ADR-0138](./docs/adr/0138-one-writer-for-the-one-on-one-queue.md))

**Implemented — frontline / mid-manager PRIMARY; every altitude that holds a 1:1 reads the same bounded queue.** The real duty: the forty minutes before a 1:1, worked from the list the person asked to raise. Frontline/mid-manager took priority because Session 186's coverage map named them next (last primary 184) and because the carried In Progress item for exactly this rung — shared automation writer retention — was the open half of ADR-0134.

**The measured gap.** ADR-0134 declared one retention policy and wired the storage layer and the agenda ledger to it, but left every WRITER open: seven modules appended with `.slice(-30)`, nine more with `.slice(-12)` / `.slice(-MAX_TOPICS)`. A person's topics sit at the front of the list, so a blind newest-wins cut deletes them first. Reproduced through the real `loadRule`: a 30-line draft lost "My mother is ill and I need to talk about leave" to one engine write, while the rule reported a queued prompt and the warnings array stayed empty.

**What was built.** `appendTalkingPoint` is now the one door: it applies the declared policy at write time and returns `appended` / `refused` / `duplicate` / `displaced` (with authorship). A refused write is a true no-op — nothing added, nothing removed — and is printed through the existing transaction warning channel, one line per person, at most three named people, remainder counted. Twenty-four modules routed through it; nine local `MAX_TOPICS` constants deleted; a refused write can no longer be reported as a queued prompt; `autopilot`'s `blocked` result and `leaderContinuityRule` / `mitigationReview`'s silent refusals now come from the writer and print the same sentence. A source-scanning guard fails any module that bounds a `talkingPoints` statement with a local `.slice(-n)`, including the multi-line idiom that made the earlier roadmap note under-count the breach by half. No collection, rule, event, action, convention, CSV scope or schema bump.

**Altitude coverage map (Session 187):** **frontline primary 187**; **mid-manager primary 187**; director last primary 186; VP last primary 186; CEO / C-suite last primary 185. Next rotation: **CEO / C-suite**.

**Verified (one focused pass).** New `agenda-queue-writers` suite **11/11**: the shared writer's append/displace/refuse/duplicate contracts, the bounded refusal channel with a counted remainder, the reproduction through the real `loadRule`, a refused write not claimed as a queued prompt, reload parity (no write-then-delete), and the source guard. Adjacent suites across the affected modules: **~500 tests**, every failure (10 across `load`, `org-network`, `parity`, `org-design`, `performance`, and the strategy/dynamics/premises/settlement schema fixtures) **re-confirmed pre-existing on the base commit via `git stash`**. `npm run lint` PASS; `npm run check:boundary` PASS (588 modules / 184 suites / 23 doc checks, 0 leaks). Full canonical suite, standalone execution and real-browser AT walkthrough **[UNVERIFIED]**.

Authorship is the registry's marker grammar, not a heuristic. Seats remain workflow declarations, not authentication.

## 2026-11-08 — The span budget exposure roll-up: money is a position per currency, an authority per branch, and a queue (Session 183, Schema v118 unchanged, [ADR-0136](./docs/adr/0136-span-budget-exposure-rollup.md), `#/finance?panel=span`)

**Implemented — director (rank 3) / VP (rank 4) PRIMARY; CEO / C-suite reads the same roll-up as counts, currency totals and bands; frontline/mid-manager are refused at the portfolio floor with the reason printed.** The real duty: a director allocating one fixed envelope across four teams, and a VP forecasting quarterly exposure across divisions. The question is not "which envelopes exist" — `#/finance` answered that — it is **"what is my span's position in each currency, which branch is carrying the overrun, and where is the ledger too unsound to forecast from?"** Director/VP took priority because the Session-182 coverage map named them the next rotation (last primary **180**, against frontline/mid 181 and CEO 182) and the Universal Hierarchy Mandate gives the most-neglected rung priority. No steering line overrode it.

**The measured gap.** `budgetsRollup(state)` maps every readable envelope to a card and counts them; nothing summed a span, nothing separated a currency above the envelope, nothing attributed an envelope to the branch that holds its authority (`budget.ownerId`), nothing bounded the review, and nothing applied the portfolio `detailCeiling` to this screen — so rank 3–4 saw item detail with no aggregate, and rank 5 saw no money at all.

**What was built.** `app/core/domain/budgetExposure.js` — a pure reader over the SAME `evaluateBudget` the terminal renders, with the same watch convention and the same day, so the position and the cards cannot disagree. Per **currency** (never pooled, never converted): envelopes, ceilings with their coverage (`n of m`), actuals, open commitments, planned pipeline, forecast at completion, breaches, watches, evidence debt, untracked. **Headroom is BLANK — never zero —** when any active envelope in that currency carries no ceiling. Every envelope is attributed to exactly one of a **direct child branch**, the **own desk**, or `unowned` / `out-of-span` / `ambiguous`, the last three counted and excluded from every total with a printed reason. A **constraint-first bounded queue** (reason family → utilisation → currency → id; 24 rows, remainder counted) names what needs a decision. The reading **refuses to net** a breach against a sibling branch's headroom, and says so. Detail is altitude-shaped: full detail at 3–4 (branch holders named — org structure the director already reads on the People screen), counts/totals/bands above the ceiling (no envelope name, no per-envelope amount), refusal below the floor. No collection, node, relation, rule, event, action, setting, convention or CSV scope; not an isolated surface — the panel sits on the existing terminal, the read is registered in `SAFE_READS` and scoped on the raw store through `canSee`, and the upward brief is identity-free by construction.

**Two defects repaired on the path, both reproduced with a probe first.** **(1)** `normalizeBudgets` used `nonNegativeOrNull`, i.e. `Number(null) === 0`, so an **absent** money field became `0` on the first reload: a spent line with no recorded actual, and an open line with no committed amount, both turned into measured zeros. `evaluateBudget`'s `missingActualLines` / `unpricedOpenCount` branches then never fired again, the RULE-FIN-03 debt prompt went quiet, and the commitment-calibration ledger scored a **fake 0× underspend** into the median a leader is asked to trust — the ADR-0130/ADR-0135 defect class, created on every save. `moneyOrNull` now keeps an absent amount absent. **(2)** The portfolio `detailCeiling` promised a chief counts-and-shares; this screen rendered nothing for rank 5 (the projection withholds the records). The aggregate now exists as currency totals, counts and bands.

**Altitude coverage map (Session 183):** frontline last primary 181; mid-manager last primary 181; **director primary 183**; **VP primary 183**; CEO / C-suite last primary 182. Next rotation: **frontline / mid-manager**.

## 2026-11-08 — The carry-forward ledger: a board pack is a series, not an event (Session 182, Schema v118 unchanged, [ADR-0135](./docs/adr/0135-board-carry-forward-ledger.md))

**Implemented — CEO / C-suite (rank 5) PRIMARY; director, VP and every lower altitude read the same ledger (the claims are enterprise assertions and the snapshot carries no person).** The real duty: the chief walking into the second board meeting of the year. The board has already been shown one frozen pack; the question is not "what do the numbers say today" but **"what moved since the pack you froze, and what is still broken?"** CEO took priority because the Session-181 coverage map left the C-suite as the most-neglected rung (last primary **179**, against frontline/mid 181 and director/VP 180), and the Universal Hierarchy Mandate gives that rung priority. No steering line overrode it.

**The measured gap.** ADR-0085 has frozen a snapshot of every board pack since Schema v91 — verdicts, point estimates, interval bounds, observation counts, declared thresholds, disclosure tags. `grep previousMemo|delta|drift` across the Board Room returns nothing: `boardRead` evaluates ONE memo live, `boardAttentionCount` reads only the newest snapshot's failing verdicts, and `boardRules` takes one frozen memo at a time. So the workspace could re-measure the enterprise every quarter and could never say what changed since the last pack.

**What was built.** `app/core/domain/boardContinuity.js` — a pure reader over `boardMemos[].snapshot`, oldest first, that derives per claim: the **transition class** between the last two looks (`separated` when the two stored Wilson (1927) 95% intervals do not overlap; `inside-noise` when they do — the verdict moved, the evidence did not; `ruler-moved` when the declared threshold changed between looks, so the movement belongs to the bar; `unclassified` when a reading carries no interval; `steady`; `first-look`), the **failing streak** and the **unproducible streak**, and a **carry-forward** flag at a declared floor of two consecutive packs, aged from the oldest look in the current unbroken carry. Bounded: the last 24 looks are read and the 40-row queue is dispatched oldest-carry-first with the remainder counted, never dropped. No p-value is printed — consecutive looks share the record they are drawn from, so interval separation is a conservative screen, not a test, and the ledger says so. No collection, node, relation, rule, event, action, setting or CSV scope; not an isolated surface — the read is computed inside the existing `boardRead` (`report.continuity`), rendered as a sixth `#/board?panel=cycle` panel with a downloadable ledger, appended to the existing identity-free `boardBriefText` consumed by Today/Signals, exported as seven additive columns on the existing `board-claims` aggregate CSV, and registered in `SAFE_READS`. The badge is deliberately unchanged.

## 2026-11-07 — Thirteen link types nobody could follow: the typed graph resolves, and a normalizer stops eating its own output (Session 176, Schema v118 unchanged, [ADR-0130](./docs/adr/0130-typed-graph-resolution-and-roundtrip.md))

**Implemented [ALL ALTITUDES — the shared graph spine, not one rung's surface].** The real duty: following a cross-module reference. A frontline lead tracing which governed decision a cover declaration opened; a mid-manager following an escalation record back to its finding; a director reading the lineage of a plan; a VP auditing an authority snapshot; a chief asking what a frozen span reading was measured on. This session took the standing `[all altitudes]` foundational item carried in every Next list since Session 172 — and specifically the *pre-existing, reproduced* 3-of-8 failure rather than a new surface. No altitude was neglected (Session-175 map: CEO 175, frontline/mid 174, director/VP 173), so the altitude-coverage rule did not force a rotation this session.

**Two live defects, both reproduced before any change.**

1. **Thirteen registered link types had no resolver case.** `LINK_ENTITY_TYPES` declares 115 first-class graph nodes; `resolveLinkedEntity` implemented 102. Unresolvable: the entire coverage family (`dutycover`, `absenceplan`, `standbyanswer`, `rehearsal`, `branchask`, `branchreading` — ADR-0121–0129) and the analytics family (`fitsnapshot`, `fitproposal`, `fitreading`, `jurfinding`, `jurreading`, `spanreading` — ADR-0109–0110). All thirteen are written onto the spine by real rules, so a propagation row naming one rendered as a broken reference **and the cross-module link CSV silently dropped the whole edge**. Thirteen cases added, each written to the same disclosure rule: the label carries the record's shape — kind, dates, state, **counts** — and never its protected content (no duty free text, no absence reason, no answerer's or recorder's words, no objective title, no member record ids, no per-person figure). The branch ask carries **no seat id and no position**, because ADR-0129 keeps seat ids off branch rows precisely so a withheld cell cannot be re-identified by walking the graph — a label that leaked one would reopen the channel the floor closed.

2. **`normalizeFitProposals` failed its own round trip.** It wrote `predictedSaving: null`, then re-read that `null` through `Number(null) === 0` as "a saving of zero with no currency", and the fail-closed normalizer correctly dropped the row. A legitimate delegation proposal **survived one load and vanished on the next**. `finite()` no longer coerces `null` / `undefined` / `''` to zero. Absent is absent.

**A case may not invent a focus the terminal cannot honour.** The coverage and analytics families resolve to the panel that OWNS the record (`#/duty-cover?panel=register|plan|readings`, `#/fit?panel=book|ladder|grade`, `#/jurisdiction?panel=options|drift`, `#/span-calibration?panel=readings`), because those panels address the record against the **acting seat** and a fabricated `?id=` would scroll to a table and highlight nothing. The premise assessment, mission capture, comparison and escalation record *do* address a frozen record by query, and those are pinned exactly.

**The sweep could not fail, and now can.** `typed-links-lineage` was recorded for four sessions as "pre-existing 3/8 on main" and left alone. Its fixture had no rows for the analytics collections and its `targetIdFor` helper *asserted* every type had one, so the test died before checking anything — the missing resolver cases and the broken round trip were both invisible behind that. It now resolves every type the fixture populates (101 of 115), reports its real coverage through `t.diagnostic`, and **pins the 14 uncovered types as a literal**, so a newly registered type cannot appear without a fixture and pass unnoticed.

**Found while building, fixed at the root.** An independent id counter made `createScorecard` collide with an id the store had just issued — the create was quietly refused and an absolute `length === 1` ledger pin only "passed" because a real transaction was missing; the fixture now shares one counter and asserts *the commit transaction it names* through backup, persistence and reload instead of counting rows. A `clearDemo` assertion looked its trace up by `entityId`, which returned the CREATE trace rather than the COMMIT trace it had scrubbed. Four route pins the sweep had never reached were added; a duplicate `carryover` pin that shadowed its own honest known-gap branch was removed.

## 2026-11-07 — The branch reading hand-off: a withheld cell is a question nobody had asked (Session 175, Schema v118, [ADR-0129](./docs/adr/0129-branch-reading-handoff.md))

**Implemented [CEO / C-suite (rank 5) PRIMARY; director and VP ask and answer the same exchange inside their own spans; mid-manager answers as the branch leader and inherits nothing above it].** The real duty: a chief reviewing cross-division strategic exposure finds one division **WITHHELD** at the disclosure floor, and still has to commit capital, people and a board narrative across the whole enterprise. Before this session the floor protected the figure by removing the signal entirely — so the chief guessed, walked the corridor, or had an analyst read the file out of band, which is the disclosure the floor exists to stop, minus the record of who asked. CEO took priority because the Session-174 coverage map put the C-suite last primary in **172** (frontline and mid-manager 174, director/VP 173), and this was the standing `[CEO → all]` Next target carried in every session since 163.

**What was missing.** ADR-0126's own flagged limitation: *"there is no in-product route from a withheld cell to that branch's own register yet."* `branchCoverage` could withhold a cell and could not accept a question about it. The branch leader who legitimately holds the numbers had **no surface in the product at all**.

**What was built.** Two stored, append-only ledgers (`branchReadingAsks`, `branchReadings`) and seven derived states. The chief addresses a **table position** ("Branch 2"), resolved inside the action against their own direct children — so no node id travels on a branch row and the schema-v114 privacy pin still holds. The branch's own leader answers with a **band computed by the register at that instant** (`holding` / `thin` / `exposed` / `unknown`) plus their own words: `branchReadingPublish` accepts **no band input at all**, so no form can type "we are fine", and the band freezes with the day it was given. The chief receives the band and the words and **no count** — the counts behind the band stay in the branch's register, which is the reason the cell was withheld. `asked` / `overdue` / `published` / `declined` / `lapsed` / `withdrawn` are DERIVED from the two ledgers and today, never stored: the ask goes overdue after `dutyCoverageReadingResponseDays` (5), a published band **lapses** after `dutyCoverageReadingValidDays` (30) because a reading about July is not a reading about September, and a **revoked** answer falls back to `asked` rather than keeping a band nobody stands behind. A **decline is an answer**: recorded, printed with its reason, counted in the brief — and it opens **no governed decision**, because a refusal that escalates itself is not a refusal.

**Wired, not bolted on.** One atomic `store.update` per act: ask → row + `requests-reading-from` edge to the branch leader + one `rolls-up-to` edge per span above the **asker** + audit event; answer → row + `answers-reading-ask` edge to the ask + one `rolls-up-to` edge per span above the **branch leader** + event. `branchask` and `branchreading` are first-class graph types in the shared link registry (`LINK_ENTITY_TYPES` / `LINK_ENTITY_COLLECTIONS` / relation vocabulary), so the hand-off rides the general propagation spine. The withheld cell carries the derived state (`branches[].reading`, plus `branchCoverage.readings` counts), the identity-free upward brief carries a counts-only line with no figure and no name, the CSV gains four per-cell columns and five summary counts (**BLANK, never 0**, for a cell nobody asked about), and `dutyCoverageAttentionCount` adds an overdue ask the acting seat **owes** and a **lapsed** reading on its own table — an ask still inside its window is a normal Monday and is not counted. Refusals are enforced twice: one level down only, requester cannot self-answer, peer cannot answer a sibling's ask, operator cannot answer at all, and the fail-closed schema drops a third-party, orphaned, pre-dated, bandless, invented-band, band-carrying-refusal or wordless answer on reload with the reason printed. Migration 117→118 is additive, convergent and starts **both ledgers empty** — no ask and no disclosure is fabricated at upgrade time.

## 2026-11-07 — Explicit cover rehearsal records: inferred work is not proof a stand-in practised the duty (Session 174, Schema v117, [ADR-0128](./docs/adr/0128-explicit-cover-rehearsal.md))

**Implemented [frontline (rank 1) / mid-manager (rank 2) PRIMARY; director and VP inherit the counts through the unchanged identity wall; CEO gets the counts-only line in the upward brief].** The real duty: a shift lead preparing a handover — and the manager who reads it — is not asking "did anyone touch this duty recently". They are asking *did this named stand-in actually practise this duty, on a dated day, with somebody who was there to see it, and what did that practice find?* Frontline and mid-manager took priority because the Session-173 coverage map put them last primary in 171 and 170 (director/VP 173, CEO 172), and this was Session 173's own tagged `[frontline → mid-manager]` Next target.

**What was missing, and why it mattered.** ADR-0125 made the exercise grade window-specific and duty-specific, but the evidence it grades is still **inferred dated work**: a cover who touched a case the week before the absence proves contact with the duty's sources, not that they practised being answerable. Meanwhile the single most informative event in the preparation window — a rehearsal run on the live board with somebody there to see it — left no artefact in the ledger at all, and a drill that stalled at the handoff was indistinguishable from one that ran clean, because neither was recorded.

**What was built.** One new stored collection, `dutyRehearsals`: the dated human act and nothing else — which cover row was rehearsed, the day it was run (bounded to the last 60 days), the mode from a declared vocabulary (`walkthrough`, `shadow`, `supervised`, `handover`), the outcome (`ready` or `gaps`), the recorder's own words, the governed decision a gaps finding opens, and append-only revocation. Everything else is derived on every read: the evidence entry, the attestation strength (`holder` / `supervisor` / `self` from the recorder against the duty holder's ancestor chain), and the grades. A `ready` rehearsal inside the preparation window grades **`rehearsed`** (exercised TRUE) above any amount of inferred work; ADR-0125's inferred evidence still grades `valid` where no drill was recorded; a rehearsal that **found gaps** grades `gaps` (exercised FALSE), holds the duty line thin, prints `FOUND GAPS` with the date, and opens a governed decision quoting the recorder verbatim with `reviewOn` pulled to the absence start. Self-reporting by the cover is allowed and permanently marked; strength beats recency when both exist.

**Wired, not bolted on.** Only **a seat that was there** attests — the holder, the named cover, or a leadership span above the holder — enforced in the action **and** by the fail-closed schema normalizer, which drops on reload any third-party, self-contradictory, pre-dated or mismatched-cover attestation with its reason printed, so a hand-edited file cannot invent an observer. Each record is ONE atomic `store.update`: the row, one `attests-rehearsal-of` edge to the cover declaration, one `rolls-up-to` edge per ancestor above the **holder**, and the audit event; `ready` opens no decision, `gaps` opens its governed decision in the same transaction. Counts travel through `absenceWindowPlan` rows (`rehearsedAvailableN` / `gapsAvailableN`), the plan summary, the concurrency `coverExercise`, the rollup reducer, `buildAbsenceSection`, `dutyAbsenceDeclare` (decision + event), `dutyAbsenceScan`, the identity-free upward brief and two new columns on the CSV's existing `absence` row kind. Above rank 2 the record id is stripped at construction (mode, outcome, attestation and counts survive — they are not identity). The plan panel gains the rehearsal ledger card with its Ready/Gaps/Revoked counts, the Rehearse act on every cover row, and the `rehearsed <day>` / `rehearsal found gaps <day>` badges; `dutyRehearsalList` is a `SAFE_READ` and `attest-duty-rehearsal` is gated rank 1–5. Migration 116→117 is additive, convergent, and starts **empty** — no attestation is ever back-filled.
