### Planned — Not Started

- **Interference-aware rollout experiment design and exposure audit [mid-manager / director / VP × single-chain and matrix]:** a leader comparing an intervention with an untreated team needs to know whether people or practices cross between the arms; in a matrix the same person may belong to both, violating the no-interference assumption and making a seemingly clean comparison misleading. Record declared intervention assignment, exposure and time windows; identify overlapping people/lines and cross-arm spillover paths using the canonical matrix DAG, count each person once per arm while explicitly flagging dual exposure, and refuse a causal-effect claim when exposure, assignment or independence is unproven. Support cluster-randomized designs where the leader declares the clusters; do not invent random assignment or infer that an unobserved contact occurred. Integrate with the existing Studies/vitals measurements and shared event spine so a change in assignments or reporting lines reopens the audit. Duty: design and interpret real change pilots without mistaking contamination for an effect. Basis: SUTVA / interference, cluster-randomized trials and causal inference. Targeted search of `app/core/domain` and the roadmap for `sutva`, `cluster.randomi[sz]`, `partial interference` and `spillover` found no such experiment-design model (other matches concern unrelated monetary spillovers or a pre/post date boundary); repository-wide absence **[UNVERIFIED]**. Discovered Session 227 (Step 3).

- **Social-choice aggregation of competing line priorities [mid-manager / director × matrix]:** the lines that share a person each rank the same work differently, and the app has no method for combining those rankings; self-declared scores (WSJF-style) reward whoever inflates them. Needed: a declared aggregation rule over the lines' ordinal rankings (a Condorcet winner where one exists, with Kemeny–Young or Schulze as the stated completion), and cycles shown as genuine disagreements routed to the lines' common leader rather than broken silently. Evidence: `condorcet|borda|kemeny|schulze` matches 0 files in `app/` (Session 226).

- **Leader Standard Work & tiered daily management [frontline / mid-manager × single-chain and matrix]:** the app tracks 1:1s, delegations and reviews but has no declared recurring routine per leadership level, no record of whether the routine was done, and no tiered escalation of what a routine check finds. Needed: a standard-work declaration per seat, done / missed evidence, missed-routine escalation to the next tier, and in a matrix which line owns each routine. Evidence: `gemba|standard work|tiered daily` matches 0 files in `app/` (Session 226).

- **Resource levelling of dated cross-line demands [frontline / mid-manager × matrix]:** when two lines place dated work on one shared person, nothing levels the load within each item's slack or says which line must move. Needed: per-person period load from dated commitments against the declared line shares, levelling within float (heijunka), and an explicit "cannot be levelled" verdict addressed to the lines' common leader. Depends on "line attribution on work records" below. Evidence: `heijunka|load-level|resource level` matches 0 files in `app/` (Session 226).

- **Per-line confidentiality of 1:1 records in a matrix [frontline / mid-manager × matrix] — BUILT Session 228 ([ADR-0165](docs/adr/0165-per-line-one-on-one-confidentiality.md), Schema v132 unchanged):** a manager who reaches a person only through a declared additional line reads the home manager's 1:1 with that person in full (`canSee` returns `full` via the line; observed on a fixture in Session 226). Needed: a declared rule for which lines may read the body of a 1:1 they did not hold, with the others seeing only that a meeting happened. The In Progress 1:1 draft adds a per-meeting holder, but does not enforce that rule; this is a merge blocker for the draft, not a shipped privacy guarantee.

- **Feedback conversation bodies are readable by any rank ≤2 seat reaching the person through a declared additional line [frontline / mid-manager × matrix]:** the same defect class ADR-0165 just closed for 1:1 meetings, unverified elsewhere: `feedback` is individual-class with a rank-2 detail ceiling, so a second-line manager at rank ≤2 reads the full situation/behaviour/impact text of the home manager's feedback conversations with a shared person — content no line needs to do its own job. Would apply the identical holder-room rule to feedback records (or declare a distinct policy deliberately), plus a fail-closed guard on feedback mutation doors. Discovered by inspection while building ADR-0165 (Session 228); repository-wide absence of any such boundary **[UNVERIFIED]**.

- **Objective / key-result dependency critical-path and float analysis [mid-manager / director / VP × single-chain and matrix]:** objectives currently carry independent key results, while the app's dependency records are not a goal/KR precedence network. A manager deciding whether to protect a milestone needs to know which upstream delay consumes schedule float, which objectives lie on the critical path, and whether a claimed finish date survives an explicit duration change. Build a typed, acyclic goal/KR dependency graph with transparent critical-path and total-float calculations, refuse cycles, missing durations or ambiguous multi-line ownership, and show branch-level roll-ups without counting a shared objective twice. Use CPM (Kelley–Walker), PERT only where three-point duration evidence exists, and a sensitivity/criticality index rather than treating a single path as certainty. Route approved dependency changes and dated critical-path crossings through the existing cross-module event/automation spine and the same matrix DAG; do not auto-resequence goals. Targeted inspection found no goal/KR dependency fields or CPM reader; broader repository-wide absence **[UNVERIFIED]**. Discovered Session 225 (Step 3).

- **Goal attainment period close and restatement ledger [VP / CEO × single-chain and matrix]:** a leader reports an on-track share upward at quarter end and the workspace keeps no record of it: attainment is always recomputed from today's records, so a later owner change, a goal re-attributed between lines, an ended line or a late check-in silently changes what last quarter "was". Finance has the control and the workspace does not — a period is CLOSED, the closing figure is kept as originally reported, and any later change is a dated, explained restatement printed beside the original (prior-period adjustment; IAS 8 / ASC 250). Would freeze, at a declared boundary, each span's aggregate attainment counts (never a person or a goal title), recompute the same period from current records, and print original, restated and the difference by cause — or refuse where the period cannot be reconstructed — rolling up through the matrix and issuing the restatement note on the shared spine; it would never overwrite a closed figure. Reuse the chain's span-reading freeze (`buildChainReading`), goal check-in history and ADR-0149 structure history. Distinct from chain readings (a forecast frozen to be graded, not an attained figure under restatement control), ADR-0158 (share-days charged) and the blocked as-of matrix-line read (structure, not attainment). Targeted greps of `app/` and `ROADMAP.md` for restatement, period close and goal or attainment snapshots found no such record; repository-wide absence **[UNVERIFIED]**. Discovered Session 224 (Step 3).

- **Credit-claiming and blame-avoidance audit over goal line stances [director / VP / CEO × matrix]:** once a line manager can state that a line carries or releases a goal (the Session 224 register, In Progress), attribution becomes something to game — claim what is on track, release what is not. Would test, in aggregate only and above a small-cell floor, whether carried and released goals differ in stated confidence at the moment of the stance (an exact 2×2 test; never a per-manager score), and surface a skewed attribution process to the span above both lines. Basis: Mayhew's credit claiming, Weaver's blame avoidance, Goodhart / Campbell. It reads a stance ledger that does not exist on `main`, so it cannot exist yet; nothing further was checked **[UNVERIFIED]**. Discovered Session 224 (Step 3).

- **Matrix line intake gate and share-day WIP ceiling [frontline / mid-manager × matrix]:** practice has a control for a line consuming more than it holds — a work-in-progress limit at the point of ADMISSION — and the workspace has none. Nothing records, when new work is taken on, which declared line is funding it and whether that line's share-days are already spent for the running period. Would record a dated intake act against a declared line and a running period (reusing ADR-0158's share-day ledger as the ceiling), refuse an intake that would breach the ceiling without an explicit human decision — accept the over-share, re-route to another line, or retune the declaration through the existing declaration/event spine — and roll breaches up through the matrix without ever re-routing or retuning automatically. Basis: kanban WIP limits and Little's Law, Goldratt's constraint logic, and the attention-based view already encoded in ADR-0160. Distinct from ADR-0160 (which reads after the fact), ADR-0158 (the declared charge) and `capacity.js` (unit utilisation). Targeted inspection of `app/core/domain` found no intake-time line gate or per-line WIP ceiling; repository-wide absence **[UNVERIFIED]**. Discovered Session 221.

- **Line attribution on work records — the prerequisite ADR-0160 exposed [all altitudes × matrix]:** allocation-to-output against work items (Session 219's item) cannot be built honestly today: a work item names the PERSON and not the line it was taken on under, so a person on three lines makes every item she touches reach all three, and `matrixWorkReach` correctly reports several `sites`. Attributing an item to one line would be an invented allocation. Would add a declared, typed attribution on work intake — a line id or a typed provenance edge recorded when the work is taken on, changing only where the item is actually mine — then let a later allocation-to-output comparison read exact per-line landings, refusing where an item carries no attribution rather than inferring one. Basis: activity-based costing's own requirement that a cost driver be recorded at the transaction, not reconstructed afterwards. Nothing in the repository records a per-item line reference; absence **[UNVERIFIED]**. Discovered Session 221 (building ADR-0160).

- **[BUILT Session 210]** Matrix line-exit reconciliation and the orphaned-obligation ledger — shipped as **Matrix Line-Exit Obligation Register** ([ADR-0152](./docs/adr/0152-matrix-line-exit-obligations.md), Schema v127, `RULE-LEX-01`, CSV #114, `#/matrix?panel=exit`). Every ended line's open obligations are printed with their age and a two-window verdict, an `after` window is flagged but never retired automatically, a carry must name a live line holder, and a line key that resolves to nothing reads `vanished` rather than being dropped. Original discovery note retained below. [frontline / mid-manager / director / VP × matrix]: when a declared line ends, every open obligation addressed to that line's manager — an onboarding brief, a review-input ask, a consent acknowledgement, a longer-running delegation — keeps its addressee and its roll-up edge while the line that justified it no longer exists. A director then reads work that structurally cannot close, and a person keeps being chased about a job they no longer hold. Would read the live matrix's inactive lines against the open obligation ledger, name each orphan with the line it belonged to and the day it ended, and route a governed remedy through the shared event spine — never silently reassigning an obligation to another manager, which would fabricate an accountability nobody accepted. Reuses the matrix engine's `inactiveLines`, the shared delegation/ask ledgers and the typed provenance path; no parallel register. Operations basis: exit-criteria hygiene and orphaned-work-in-process accounting. Targeted inspection found that line consent (ADR-0148) records an ended DECLARATION and structure history (ADR-0149) records a moved HOME line, but nothing reconciles the WORK addressed to a line that no longer exists; repository-wide absence **[UNVERIFIED]**. Discovered Session 208.



- **In Progress — term-exposure slice implemented Session 214; two-sided re-affirmation outstanding. Matrix line sunset and two-sided re-affirmation — the term of office a declared line was never given [frontline / mid-manager / director × matrix]:** ADR-0148 records an INITIAL answer on a declared line and ADR-0152 settles what a line leaves behind when it ENDS, but nothing gives a line a **term**. A project line declared "until further notice" that has run three years has never been re-affirmed by either manager or the person, and its allocation is inherited forever because no act ever revisited it. Would read each declared line's declared term (or its absence) against a printed convention, flag `no-term-declared` / `reaffirmation-due` / `reaffirmation-overdue` as structural findings on the **LINE** (never a person rating), and require a dated, two-sided reconfirmation of the CURRENT share by the managers and the person before the line may continue past its term — refusing to renew silently, and never treating the original consent as consent to today's number. Draws on sunset-clause governance (Madisonian sunset provisions), Goold & Campbell's matrix design criteria (clarity of duration as a design variable) and the permanent-versus-temporary matrix literature (Hardy 1994). Targeted search found no line-term or re-affirmation model anywhere in the repository; absence **[UNVERIFIED]** repository-wide. Discovered Session 210.

- **[matrix, all altitudes]** Attribution integrity: does the declared allocation match the recorded work? (Discovered Session 189, not built.) The Matrix Accountability Ledger records what two managers *agreed*; it does not check it against what the workspace already knows. Every dated commitment, delegation, case and capacity entry already says where a person's time actually went. Reading the declared split against that record turns "the shares add up" into "the shares are true" — Cobb–Douglas-style allocation auditing applied to attention rather than capital. It is the difference between a register leaders fill in once and one they can be held to. Not built this session because it needs a declared policy for what counts as evidence of a person's time *on a line*, and guessing that policy would be the exact failure this product refuses to commit.
- **[matrix, all altitudes]** Matrix line acceptance: a declared share is an ask until someone accepts it. (Discovered Session 190, not built.) ADR-0140 lets one manager declare that another holds 40% of a person, and ADR-0141 lets that manager then read the work — but nobody has ACCEPTED anything. In real matrix practice the failure mode is *shadow accountability*: the project manager is nominally at 40% of an engineer she has never agreed a delivery with, the engineer was never told, and the home manager still plans her at 100%. The product already knows how to do this: ADR-0127 made a declared cover an ASK with an answer (`declared` → `accepted` / `declined` / `lapsed`) and ADR-0128 required the rehearsal before the absence. The same protocol belongs on a reporting line: manager-side acceptance of the share and its decision rights, person-side acknowledgement of "I am on the hook to these people for these hours", an expiry that lapses an unaccepted line into a printed state rather than a silent one, and a capacity check that refuses an acceptance the person's other lines cannot physically absorb (a person cannot accept 140%). Not built this session because it needs a decision about what an *unaccepted* line still does: the honest answer is that it keeps its read scope (the work is real) and loses its capacity claim (the commitment is not) — and that choice changes ADR-0141's reconciliation, so it must be made deliberately, in the open, with its own ADR. Practice basis: consent-based RACI; French & Raven's distinction between assigned and accepted authority; the "accountability without authority" literature.
- **[matrix, all altitudes]** A matrix-safe `responsibleNodeId`. (Discovered Session 189, not built.) `RULE-MTX-01` currently fans work to every manager and reports the ambiguity, which is honest but not yet *useful*: the addressee still has to work out which of them decides. The next step is a declared tie-break policy — by line kind, by decision right, by time-span of discretion (Jaques) — surfaced as a recommendation the human confirms, never an automatic owner. A silent owner is a decision the system is not entitled to make; a *proposed* owner with the reason printed is a decision the system is entitled to support.
- **[all altitudes]** A capacity-contention surface for shared people. (Discovered Session 189, not built.) The ledger answers "is this person over-committed on paper". It does not yet answer "what does 140% cost us in lead time" — Kingman's approximation applied to a person whose queue is fed from three directions. `capacity.js` and `orgDesign.js` already price utilisation as waiting time for a *unit*; nobody prices it for a person who belongs to several.
- **[all altitudes]** Server-side authorization and tenant isolation on every read, write and export, with explicit-consent data migration and independent security review.
- **[all altitudes]** A complete cross-module event catalogue audit: prove every module subscribes through the generalized engine and no rule-owned edge is written by hand.
- **[frontline → CEO]** Prospective calibration ledger for every altitude's recommendations: freeze the recommendation, grade the outcome, and report Brier/confidence intervals without rating persons.
- **[all altitudes]** Real-browser and assistive-technology verification of every new panel, plus performance testing at scale.

### Rejected (with one-line reason)

- **[all altitudes]** Claiming production RBAC or predictive individual risk from a self-declared browser seat — neither identity nor calibration is established.
- **[all altitudes]** LLM-generated financial certainty — no causal validity and no auditable derivation.
- **[all altitudes]** Automatic people decisions from case narratives — unvalidated harm and bias outweigh speculative benefit.
- **[all altitudes]** Implicit 1:1 FX conversion — false precision; mixed currencies stay unpooled.
- **[all altitudes]** Another stand-alone dashboard instead of guarding existing decision paths — duplicates the surface without closing the trust gap.

## Session 131 outcome — 2026-11-04: The Subtraction Test — a withheld cell that could be recovered by arithmetic (no schema bump, no new rule, [ADR-0091](docs/adr/0091-aggregate-determinacy.md), `#/disclosure`)

**The gap.** The roadmap's [director → CEO] In Progress item said a small child span could be recovered by subtracting it from a parent aggregate. It was worse than a gap: it was live. With one sub-floor cell and one printed cell the aggregate skipped complementary suppression entirely (`visible.length > 1` was false) and the published total returned the withheld value — `7 − 6 = 1`, `57 − 48 = 9`. Reproduced against the shipped code before any work started.

**What shipped.** `aggregateDeterminacy.js`: the published surface modelled exactly (printed cells as constants, withheld cells as integer boxes, each printed total as one equation) with closed-form exact recoverability and no floating point; a planner that hides the smallest surviving cell first and withholds the total only when no partner can help (the 4/4/4 saturation a counting rule cannot see); and an independent audit that re-checks the figures as they are about to print. `moduleAggregate` now decides through the guard and returns `guard { verdict, recoverableN, inconsistentN, checkedMeasures, line }`; the console subtitle reads `N cell(s) withheld, 0 recoverable by subtraction`, the notes and the downloaded brief carry the same sentence. **No stored shape, setting, rule, collection or CSV scope changed** — a read model moved, so `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 95.

**Altitudes served.** Frontline and team lead (the one-person span is no longer countable from above), manager and director (a child span is no longer recoverable from the parent total they were handed), VP/executive (the aggregate they read states its own recoverability), chief (the brief carries the proof, not an assurance).

**Frameworks encoded.** Statistical disclosure control: the minimum-2 rule per published marginal, complementary suppression, box-bounded integer determinacy, and the "total vs detail" trade made explicit; exact integer arithmetic rather than heuristics.

**Honest limits.** This closes the VERTICAL axis. Reorganisation comparability across a freeze line is DONE (Session 139, ADR-0099); the `lastCarriageOn` timing disclosure on suppressed rows is closed in view, snapshots and CSV. Extremum statistics (`oldestDays` is a max) are outside the additive model and are documented, not claimed safe. Other modules' local small-cell rules (`#/escalation`, `#/measurement`, `#/cadence`, `#/concordance`, `#/survival`) are not routed through this guard yet — `[UNVERIFIED]` individually.

**Next.** (1) Route the other modules' suppression through the same guard. (2) Temporal differencing over a repeated-release line. (3) Authenticated identity / tenant boundary (still the top [all altitudes] item).

## Session 130 outcome — 2026-11-04: Programme Federation — which declared edges actually carry work (Schema v95, [ADR-0090](docs/adr/0090-programme-federation.md), `RULE-FED-01..03`, CSV #86, `#/federation`)

**The gap.** Every module so far read the hierarchy from a DECLARATION. Nothing measured whether the declared edge above a span was used. A tree in which no artefact crosses an edge is an org chart, not a connected system — and the [VP → CEO] Planned item had sat unbuilt across two sessions.

**What shipped.** `#/federation` with five panels and five altitude-specific decisions. Every leadership edge is measured from five declared channels — attested packet carriage (`RULE-ENV-01`), frozen renewal readings (`RULE-SCR-01`), accepted Catchball commitments (`RULE-HK-01`), closed two-sided expectation rounds (`RULE-ECN-01`), frozen cadence readings (`RULE-CAD-01`) — and classified **direct / bypass / stale / silent / root**. Coverage is published with a Wilson 95% interval and WITHHELD below a declared span floor; rank 3+ suppresses small cells with a complementary cell. `RULE-FED-01` rolls a frozen reading to every ancestor in the same transaction, `RULE-FED-02` opens exactly one governed carriage decision per edge per ISO week (owned at the span ABOVE the edge), and `RULE-FED-03` records a reconnection **without** closing the human decision. Schema v95 adds two empty, identity-reduced ledgers and clamped conventions only; **71 rules / 71 contracts**; CSV #86 is aggregate-only.

**Altitudes served.** Frontline (did my work reach my lead, and what did not), manager (which of my spans are silent or bypassed), director (is the line above me real, or is work arriving from above it), executive (bounded programme coverage with a refusal below the floor and complementary suppression), chief (counts by altitude and channel; no span or person named).

**Frameworks encoded.** Jaques' time span of discretion as the unit of analysis; Beer's VSM requisite information channel; Burt's structural holes for the `bypass` state; the Wilson score interval; statistical disclosure control (small-cell + complementary suppression, minimum-aggregate refusal); DMAIC measurement-system analysis (the screen measures the measurement system, not the people).

**Honest limits.** A seat is still a local declaration, not authentication. The reading sees only this workspace's ledgers: carriage that happens outside LeadOS reads as silent, and the screen says so before its numbers. Suppression is not differential privacy and the new per-altitude series re-opens the temporal-differencing item below.

**Next.** (1) Temporal disclosure testing for repeated federation releases. (2) The cross-module event catalogue audit. (3) Real-browser/AT verification of the two newest panels.

## Session 129 outcome — 2026-11-04: Strategy Renewal Bridge — a frozen learning line across five operating altitudes (Schema v94, [ADR-0089](docs/adr/0089-strategy-renewal-bridge.md), `RULE-SCR-01..02`, CSV #85)

**The gap.** The Catchball cascade could negotiate and price strategy deployment, but did not preserve which commitments and bets were in scope at a review date, grade that exact cohort later, or give each altitude a distinct renewal decision.

**What shipped.** `#/strategy-cycle` freezes prospective identity-reduced readings, links the exact cohort to Catchball, bets and leadership ancestors, and presents five altitude-specific playbooks. The historical delivery reference is not called a prediction; Brier is withheld without explicit-confidence evidence; ranks 3+ receive cell suppression and complementary redaction. The director scenario is display-only. Human decisions and Catchball consent remain required: no bet, budget, owner, date or pact is auto-changed. Schema v94 adds empty prospective cycle/marker ledgers and defaults only; CSV #85 exports the active-seat report. The raw cycle and marker collections stay out of declared-seat projections, while the Disclosure Compiler opens the custom scoped report adapter.

**Honest limits.** Seats are local declarations, not authentication. Cell suppression is not differential privacy, repeated-release/reorganization differencing remains open, and the LEI strategy-deployment page was not verified for a specific claim. Vendor pages are treated as vendor-described capabilities, not independent product verification.

**Next.** Validate the five decisions with users; strengthen settlement/data-quality signals; review repeated-release privacy; and close the authenticated identity/tenant boundary.

## Session 128 outcome — 2026-11-04: The Federated Envoy — the hierarchy leaves the browser (Schema v93, no bump of its own, ADR-0088, `RULE-ENV-01..03`, CSV #84)

**The gap.** Every module so far — chain, seat, mandate, catchball, concordance, board, disclosure, cadence — models the hierarchy *inside one store*. Real organisations are not one store, and leadership work crosses workspace boundaries daily. Until now it crossed them as a document with no provenance, no disclosure scope and no way to record disagreement except a merge.

**What shipped.** `#/envoy`: five panels; packets projected by disclosure class at the source; SHA-256 per item → Merkle root → identity → HMAC (keyed required by default) with typed failures; idempotent ingest into attested copies that never edit the local record; `RULE-ENV-01` carriage to every ancestor in the same transaction; `RULE-ENV-02` one reconciliation decision per record per ISO week; `RULE-ENV-03` attested-exposure review above a declared floor and a marker below it. **69 rules / 69 contracts**, aggregate-only CSV #84, identity-free certificate. Registered as one `disclosureManifests` row and three `RECORD_POLICIES` rows, so the ADR-0086 compiler places `#/envoy` for a declared seat instead of withholding it.

**Altitudes served.** Frontline/team lead (what the altitude above may hold, and what is withheld), manager (compose to own span or leader, verdicts and divergences), director (coverage and both hashes), VP/executive (Wilson-bounded coverage refused below five spans, keyed-signature share, no titles), CEO/chief (certificate + CSV).

**Honest limits.** Not authentication (the seat is a declaration), not encryption (detail is refused, not hidden), cannot prove a foreign record is true, and a keyed exchange needs the same session key on both sides arranged out of band.

**Next up.** (1) A two-workspace key rendezvous that keeps the local-first promise — the honest prerequisite for keyed mode at scale. (2) Temporal disclosure testing for repeated packet releases (differencing a series of aggregates), now that ADR-0086 made every screen posture-aware and ADR-0087 made the aggregate a read model. (3) A programme-level federation reading: which spans are actually connected to the span above them, measured from carriage rather than declared.
## 2026-11-04 — Session 128: the position design, not the person in it (Schema v95, [ADR-0089](docs/adr/0089-operating-model.md), `#/operating-model`, RULE-OMD-01..03, CSV #83)

**The gap this closes.** LeadOS could price *waiting* (ADR-0053), *decision latency* (ADR-0043), the *promise book* (ADR-0073), the *attention market* (ADR-0047) and the *reliability of a rating instrument* (ADR-0069/0083) — and it had no reading at all of the thing all of that work is done from: **the design of the position holding it**. Every terminal asked what a leader should *do*; none asked whether the seat they are doing it from is drawable at all. That is the one question the whole org-design category answers for the CHRO with a six-figure programme and answers for a frontline manager with nothing.

**Implemented, tagged by altitude**

- **[frontline]** Span detail: four declared work-type percentages per level, a utilisation bar whose declared ceiling is **drawn on it**, and the measured overhead the position actually carries (cadence hours per report + supervision hours per open delegation). Displacement is derived from each record's own clock (`requiredRank` vs the owner's altitude), not from a self-report.
- **[manager]** The constraint, diagnosed: *over-routed* (a decision-rights defect), *over-spanned* (Mann's contingency, above the declared 3–8 band) or *over-committed* (the work itself). Each over-ceiling span gets one governed design decision per ISO week, addressed to the ancestor whose altitude can author the change.
- **[director]** Span rates and the bottleneck ranking; the **lever book** ranked by hours relieved per unit of design cost, with every continuity-unsafe option marked; the cross-unit seam share and the Graicunas combinatorial ceiling beside it.
- **[VP / executive]** One aggregate row per level below the reader (skippable spans are amortised, never exposed); attributable labour cost as a *share of a declared rate*, with the below-latitude portion separated out; abstention flow out of large units.
- **[CEO / chief]** Aggregate CSV #83 and the identity-free brief: counts, rates, gates and lever families — no person, position title, span label or individual hour.
- **[all altitudes]** Gauge R&R *on the model itself* before any figure is stated: denominator floor, arithmetic check on every declared split, and an impossible-week audit that reports over-commitment rather than trimming it. Additive `MIGRATIONS[93]`, fail-closed normalizers, 64/64 rule-contract parity, pausable auto-propagation with an always-available explicit scan.

**The lever book is the point.** Nine named structural patterns (Little's law, decision-rights simplification, route decomposition, adding a lead, boundary redraw, re-baselining, de-hubbing, a raised book ceiling, removing a relay layer), ranked arithmetically. A **hire is never the first answer** and is *refused outright* for a span below the continuity floor — because below that floor one absence stops the work, so relieving a thin span with a person makes the fragility worse. That inversion is the feature no capacity tool in the category ships.

**Framework stack encoded:** Jaques' time-span of discretion (1956/1964); Rummler–Brache determinants of performance (1990/1995); Drucker's management by self-control (1954); Senge/Forrester causal loops (1961/1990); Mann's contingent span (1965) and Graicunas (1933) / Urwick (1956) as *declared bands*; Kingman (1961) queueing at the utilisation ceiling; Shingo SMED internal/external (1985); Little (1961); Littler/Levering/Walton (1982) and Kim & Mauborgne (2003) on tolerance ≠ capacity; Hackman's authorable enabling conditions (2002); Morris critical path (1966) for continuity; MSA gauge R&R (AIAG & VDA 2010) applied to the model's own inputs; Hersey–Blanchard maturity for the frontline reading.

**Deliberately rejected:** reading a calendar (that is an attendance product); inferring the work-type split (a precise-looking figure resting on nothing is worse than a refusal); recommending a hire on utilisation alone; scoring managers on congruence (a boolean with a printed threshold is auditable, a percentage is a league table); one composite "operating health" index (hides the dimension that makes a lever choosable); per-person declarations (turns the screen into a clock).

**Next 1–3 ambitious targets**

- **Next 1 — [all altitudes] Authenticated identity + tenant boundary.** Unchanged and still the honest limit named in every recent ADR. This module adds a fourth way altitude enters the transaction, which makes it more urgent: a declared seat is a workflow boundary, not a security one.
- **Next 2 — [manager → CEO] Per-position salary band integration for attributable cost.** Today the cost is a declared rate × hours. The honest next step is the existing `compBands`/`meritCycles` enterprise material, joined at executive rank only, with the cross-currency refusal this codebase already enforces.
- **Next 3 — [frontline → director] A declared *steady-state* baseline per position.** The model can say a position is over its week; it cannot yet say whether that is a bad month or the design. A rolling baseline of committed hours per station, with a control-chart band, would let the levers be triggered on a signal instead of a snapshot.
## 2026-11-04 — Session 129: The Attested Commit ([ADR-0089](docs/adr/0089-attested-commit.md), Schema v95, `#/identity`, RULE-IDN-01..03, CSV #84)

- **Implemented [all altitudes]:** The Attested Commit (`#/identity`) — the answer to the one limit every ADR since ADR-0076 has printed ("seats are declared lenses, not authentication"). A passphrase-derived, memory-only per-seat credential (PBKDF2, public half stored: salt + 16-hex fingerprint + HMAC verifier) whose HMAC-SHA256 attests every operational commit: `entityId = HMAC(key, "leados-seat-attest-v1|seat|keyId|revision|digest")`, the digest covering every event the transaction appended before the attestation, with `sealRule` (absolutely last) covering the attestation in turn — assurance rungs 1 + 2 compose inside one atomic transaction. The enrollment commit is itself the credential's first attested act.
- **Implemented [frontline / manager]:** Enroll → unlock → sign → lock as self-service on your own seat; wrong passphrase fails closed and is audited (`identity.unlock_failed`, throttled 5 per seat per 10 minutes — the correct passphrase waits out the cooldown too); idle expiry stops attesting instead of lying; session-lifecycle events are never flagged unattributed.
- **Implemented [director]:** RULE-IDN-02 — under enforcement, a write with no unlocked credential logs `identity.unattributed` and opens **one** governed authorship-boundary DACI decision per seat per ISO week, with typed `rolls-up-to` edges to every leadership ancestor in the same transaction (frontline → manager → director → VP → chief, zero re-entry). Governing the boundary (enforcement on/off, credential revocation) is the director+ `govern-attestation` right; a manager cannot switch enforcement off on their own authority. RULE-IDN-02 is pausable; an explicit scan always surfaces the gap.
- **Implemented [VP / executive]:** Three-valued verification — verified / **FAILED** / **digest-verified · key unavailable** (never upgraded, never punished) / evicted — rolled up the chain of command with peer detail hidden behind the seat boundary (`scopeIdentitySpans` collapse), and a nav badge counting failures + unattributed writes, never compliance.
- **Implemented [CEO / chief]:** Assurance rung 3: signed checkpoint documents kept **outside** the workspace detect TRUNCATED / REWOUND / REWRITTEN a self-referential chain cannot see; the HMAC binds the document body; unsigned checkpoints say `UNSIGNED` out loud. Identity-free brief and aggregate-only CSV #84 (`seat-attestation`) leak no seat id, name, fingerprint or MAC; attestation rate below the 5-transaction floor is blank, never 0.
- **Enforcement:** the ADR-0080 gateway fails closed — `identityEnforced` refuses every non-exempt write without a session; boundary management (enroll/unlock/lock) stays reachable so the gate can never lock anyone out of managing the boundary itself.
- **Next 1 — [all altitudes] Authenticated identity + tenant boundary.** Server-side authorization on every read/write/export; the credential is accountable authorship inside one browser, not authentication of a human being.
- **Next 2 — [director → CEO] Reviewed legacy-module adapters + temporal disclosure.** Carry the disclosure floor across repeated releases (differencing over time) and give the remaining legacy views reviewed seat-scoped adapters.
- **Next 3 — [manager → CEO] Outcome learning for authorship posture.** Grade whether authorship-boundary decisions taken per seat per week actually close the gaps they opened (Brier/base-rate on the workspace's own record), without rating persons.
- **Rejected [all altitudes]:** ECDSA auditor signatures (no PKI without a second party), RFC 3161 external timestamping (network violates local-first), rounding "key unavailable" up to "verified", storing anything key-shaped in the workspace, pausing attestation during automation freezes.

## 2026-11-04 — Session 129: The Hoshin Carryover Terminal ([ADR-0089](docs/adr/0089-hoshin-carryover-terminal.md), Schema v95, `#/carryover`, RULE-CO-01..04, CSV #84)

**The gap this closes.** Session 124 could *detect* a thesis-invalidated pact — faithful execution against a falsified upstream hypothesis — but not **settle** it. The bet was never judged against its stop rule, the encumbered person-days and budget line evaporated instead of re-entering the next allocation cycle, and no dated prediction was frozen so the settlement could ever be graded. The 2026 strategy-execution market renders invalidation as a status change; nobody models it as a settlement event.

- **[Frontline / team lead]** The invalidated pact's settlement record, the resource bundle frozen at invalidation, and the settlement decision to answer — with the bundle printed in the question.
- **[Manager]** Settlement queue across the span: awaiting verdict, release in flight, released, withheld (with the written reason).
- **[Director]** Judge the bet against its stop rule: retire, revise the stop rule, or reaffirm with a new causal hypothesis. Unresolved bet bases surface as defects.
- **[VP / executive]** Bets and stop rules with their state; the portfolio question — what did this falsification release for the next allocation cycle?
- **[CEO / chief]** Altitude calibration cells (n, hold rate, Wilson 95% bounds), aggregate invalidation and released-capacity totals, and an identity-free brief.

**Next targets.** (1) Cross-cycle carryover *forecasting* — price next cycle's expected released capacity before the settlements land, so the allocation governor can plan against it rather than discover it. (2) A stop-rule quality index: distinguish a span whose stop rules hold because it judges well from one whose stop rules hold because it bets safely. (3) Authenticated identity — every seat here is a declaration, not an account.

## 2026-11-04 — Session 128: The Escalation Economy ([ADR-0088](docs/adr/0088-escalation-economy.md), Schema v94, `#/escalation`, RULE-ESC-01..05, CSV #83)

**The gap this closes.** The 2026 market sells "escalation management" and means ticket routing (ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, PagerDuty, Zendesk, HaloITSM; AI entrants Fini, Forethought, Traversal, Ada) — *who gets paged next, how fast*, with reason-clustering analytics. LeadOS was closer and still short: `load.js` measures cognitive load on a person, `signalPath.js` measures bad-news transmission up declared channels, `mandates.js` records who may decide. None of them measured the **escalation decision** — the moment a leader absorbs a problem or hands it up — its price, its yield, or the incentive that produced it. This session prices that market.

**Implemented, tagged by altitude**

- **[frontline]** Absorb-or-escalate logging with a reason vocabulary that makes the incentive visible (`cover` and `capacity` counted as defensive), and the **monkey ledger** of what I have sent upward and how long it has been gone.
- **[manager]** The receiving span as an **M/M/1 service station** — arrivals, utilisation, Kingman-bounded waiting time, absorption headroom, and a refusal instead of a large number at ρ ≥ 1 — plus return-the-monkey actions and the intervention-rate commitment I am graded against.
- **[director]** Escalation hotspots across managers, the **subsidiarity index** per decision class, the de facto centralisation map, and the escalation tax in person-days.
- **[VP / executive]** Portfolio of queue utilisation across spans and the escalation tax in the declared currency.
- **[CEO / chief]** Enterprise escalation topology, graded commitments with Brier skill, and an identity-free board-ready brief.
- **[all altitudes]** Exact-partition roll-up (a record counts once at the span where it arose and is inherited by ancestors by addition), small-cell withholding, marker-idempotent and pausable automation, and receiver-only settlement so the yield is never self-reported.

**Framework stack encoded:** Aghion & Tirole (1997) *Formal and Real Authority*; Holmström & Milgrom (1991) multitask principal–agent; Jensen & Meckling (1995) and the principle of subsidiarity; Erlang M/M/1 and Kingman (1961); Shannon (1948) binary symmetric channel cascade; Oncken & Wass (1974) *Who's Got the Monkey?*; Wilson (1927); Brier (1950).

**Deliberately rejected:** inferring whether the outcome differed from a title, note or resolution code (it is a human judgement and the only input the yield rests on); ranking or scoring escalating individuals (the instrument for the incentive problem is the reason vocabulary and the commitment, not a leaderboard); auto-returning an escalation; printing any waiting time at ρ ≥ 1; a single composite "escalation health score" that would hide the class-level and span-level finding.

**Next 1–3 ambitious targets**

- **Next 1 — [all altitudes] Authenticated identity + tenant boundary.** Still the one honest limit that appears in every recent ADR. Carried forward unchanged in priority.
- **Next 2 — [manager → CEO] Cross-span horizontal escalation.** Extend the vertical absorb-or-escalate ledger with **lateral** hand-offs between peer spans, arbitrated at their lowest common ancestor, so supplier–customer escalations are priced like vertical ones.
- **Next 3 — [director → CEO] Escalation market simulation.** A counterfactual engine: re-solve the last period under a different intervention-rate commitment and grade the simulated queue, tax and yield against what was recorded — the same freeze/grade discipline, applied to a policy the leader did not choose.

## 2026-11-04 — Session 126: the catalogue opens, and the boundary proves itself (Schema v92, [ADR-0086](docs/adr/0086-disclosure-compiler.md), `#/disclosure`, RULE-DSC-01..02)

**The gap this closes.** The enforced boundary shipped in ADR-0076 refused 84 of 89 routes under a declared seat, pending a per-screen read audit. Three sessions in a row listed "reviewed adapters, one module at a time" as the follow-up, and three sessions discovered why that plan could not finish: the queue grew with the catalogue. The result was a hierarchy model nobody could work in — the exact failure §0.3 of the mandate names.

**Implemented, tagged by altitude**

- **[all altitudes]** `#/disclosure` — the console: coverage of all 96 screens with the posture each holds here and the reason, the compiled aggregate read, the release ledger, and an identity-free upward brief. Aliases `visibility`, `access`, `posture`, `who-sees-what`, `small-cell`.
- **[frontline / team lead]** Every frontline screen renders in detail inside its window (`1:1s`, feedback, conflicts, goals, delegations, cases, decisions, people, growth, readiness, onboarding, reviews, prep, health) — no more nav that shows three items. Portfolio and enterprise classes stay withheld **below** their floor, with the reason.
- **[manager]** Record-level detail up to the individual ceiling, unit work in detail, and a compiled count of exactly what the boundary withheld from this seat (the badge counts the boundary, never "work to do").
- **[director]** Unit work in detail; individual classes roll up to per-span counts and rates with the floor applied; capital/finance in detail; enterprise classes withheld below rank 4.
- **[VP / executive]** Portfolio terminal classes publish their aggregate under a declared seat rather than a refusal page: records, open, overdue, severity load, oldest age, money per currency, per-child-span rows, complementary suppression, and an explicit statement of what the terminal's own report reads cannot yet scope.
- **[CEO / chief]** Every class as counts at the top of the tree, with the money question answered per currency and the individual question answered without a single note, name or rating.
- **[all altitudes]** A **release contract**: request → span-leader consent → 1–30 day window → one screen, one span, one seat; expiry swept by `RULE-DSC-02`; `enterprise` classes never releasable; floors never liftable; per-seat cap and duplicate refusal; requested/consented/refused/revoked/expired all auditable and prompted.
- **[engineering]** 97 manifests, one compiler, 67/67 rule-contract parity, additive `MIGRATIONS[91]`, two collections (`disclosureGrants`, `disclosureMarkers`), five clamped settings, four new/unlocked typed links (`disclose-to`, `consented-by`, plus node `disclosuregrant`), and one leak-oracle suite that navigates every route at four seats.

**Framework stack encoded:** attribute-based access control as a *compile* rather than hand-written adapters; statistical disclosure control — small-cell suppression with **complementary suppression** and total suppression below the floor (Federal Committee on Statistical Methodology / cell-suppression practice); principal–agent consent over data disclosure (the span that owns the record consents, not the requester); Jaques' time span of discretion as the reason the unit of analysis changes with altitude; fail-closed defaults (`unknown` ≠ zero, undeclared = withheld).

**Deliberately rejected:** per-module adapters written one per session (the queue grows faster than it drains); opening everything and relying on the record projection (a refusal is a lie by omission above a ceiling); letting the requester consent to their own release (self-service disclosure); release-as-a-setting (no owner, no purpose, no expiry, no grade); differential privacy claims (this is cell suppression and says so).

**Next 1–3 ambitious targets**

- **Next 1 — [all altitudes] Seat-scoped report reads for the analytic terminals.** ~45 terminals publish an aggregate today because their report reads scan the whole workspace. Bring each family's read model inside the span (as the Altitude Router and Seal already are), move it from `aggregate` to `adaptive`, and let the console's coverage number rise honestly as each one lands.

## 2026-11-04 — Session 125: the disclosure memo as an instrument that can fail (Schema v93, [ADR-0087](docs/adr/0085-board-room.md), `#/board`, RULE-BRD-01..03, CSV #82)

**The gap this closes.** `chainRegistry.js` gave the chief a `board` duty and `successionRegistry.js` a `board-line` relationship, but `#/board` rendered nothing: a promised surface with no implementation, which is worse than an absent one because it tells a reader the evidence exists. The workspace could compute enterprise figures (bench, promises, authority, concordance, health, seal) and had no honest way to put seven of them in front of a board without averaging them.

**Implemented, tagged by altitude**

- **[frontline]** Which claim of mine is failing, by how much, and what it costs — read-only; no memo may be committed from this rank.
- **[manager]** The span partition for any attributable claim, with the parts reconciled against the claim's own denominator and the arithmetic printed rather than summarised.
- **[director]** Named span rows, the worst row identified, and the delegation that a failing span actually receives (opened by `RULE-BRD-01` in the same transaction, capped at `min(60, boardRecheckDays)` days).
- **[VP / executive]** Cross-module discrepancies with both numbers and a route to the module that owns the other half; the settling-sample arithmetic; the refusal count.
- **[CEO / chief]** Pre-registration and commit: thresholds declared before the first recorded look, a content fingerprint per look, verdicts decided by the conservative end of a Wilson interval, a deterministic identity-free memorandum, attestation state, and aggregate-only CSV #82. `commit-board-memo` is rank 5–5.
- **[all altitudes]** Refusals, withholding, inconclusiveness and staleness are printed states with reasons; a refused figure is blank in every export and never zero; post-hoc threshold movement is permanent (`revisedAfterLook`); additive `MIGRATIONS[89]`, fail-closed normalizers, 67/67 rule-contract parity, pausable auto-propagation with an always-available explicit scan.

**Analytic content encoded.** Wilson (1927) score intervals with the conservative-end decision rule; the settling-sample inversion (`boardRequiredSample`), including the deliberate `null` for a claim exactly on its threshold; the DACI decision-rights model applied to a failing claim rather than to a person; disclosure-class enforcement (ADR-0075/0080) at the enterprise altitude; falsifiability as a UI constraint (Kerr 1998 on HARKing as the failure mode being designed out).

**Deliberately rejected:** a composite "board readiness score"; reporting a point estimate with a confidence note; a live dashboard rendered at memo-view time (the pack must not change after it is read); auto-correcting a failing claim; a new graph node (the memo's relationships are the existing `rolls-up-to` span edges).

**Cross-altitude proof shipped this session.** One committed memo with a failing claim produces, in a single atomic transaction: one governed DACI decision at the chief altitude, one delegation to the failing span's holder, and typed `rolls-up-to` edges to every leadership ancestor — asserted in `tests/app/board-room.test.mjs`.

**Next 1–3 ambitious targets**

- **Next 1 — [all altitudes] Authenticated identity + tenant boundary.** Still the one honest limit named in every recent ADR; a chief-only commit rule enforced against a *declared* seat is not authentication.
- **Next 2 — [director → CEO] Temporal disclosure of the memo itself.** A pack republished every quarter is a repeated release; complementary suppression across quarters, split/merge and phased-access tests have not been written.
- **Next 3 — [manager → VP] Claim-level instrument validation.** Seven claims and their default thresholds are a chosen instrument; the next step is outcome-grading each claim's threshold against decisions the workspace later made, so the instrument is calibrated rather than merely declared.

## 2026-11-04 — Session 123: the review's instrument, audited (Schema v89, [ADR-0083](docs/adr/0083-expectation-concordance.md), `#/concordance`, RULE-ECN-01..03, CSV #78)

**The gap this closes.** LeadOS could audit the *reliability of a leader's ratings over time* (ADR-0069) and the *authority of a span over an action class* (ADR-0079), but not the oldest defect in performance management: two people using different gauges for the same word. "Meets expectations" is six expectations, and nothing in the category — or in this workspace — measured whether the two people in the room meant the same thing by it. This session ships that measurement.

**Implemented, tagged by altitude**

- **[frontline]** `#/concordance` — one round per leader → report pair; both sides answer six declared dimensions independently; nothing is revealed until both are in; a sealed side cannot be revised; a closed round is evidence. Pair detail, both gauges, the gap per dimension and a deterministic conversation script (no model, no inference).
- **[manager]** Sealed-round queue (what is waiting on whom), per-pair κ trends across cycles, and one generated agenda line placed on the pair's most recent 1:1 by `RULE-ECN-02`.
- **[director]** Span rates with exact partitioning, the org-wide **dimension profile** (which word diverges, in which direction, in how many pairs), and small-cell withholding below the declared floor. Other spans' two gauges are withheld — the leader's own pairs stay readable.
- **[VP / executive]** Pairs-above-floor share with a Wilson 95% interval and a 10th–90th percentile range; one governed DACI re-contracting decision per pair per ISO week on divergence; typed `rolls-up-to` edges to every ancestor in the same transaction.
- **[CEO / chief]** Identity-free brief and aggregate-only CSV #78. No person, pair, span name, note or individual rating survives the boundary.
- **[all altitudes]** Closed loop: a second round after re-contracting is compared with breached-but-not-re-contracted pairs, printed as an **association** and refused below the cell floor. Additive `MIGRATIONS[88]`, fail-closed normalizers, 67/67 rule-contract parity, pausable auto-propagation with an always-available explicit scan.

**Framework stack encoded:** MSA / gauge R&R (AIAG & VDA 2010); quadratic weighted κ (Cohen 1968); Gwet's AC1 (2008); PABAK (Byrt, Bishop & Carlin 1993); Bland–Altman bias and limits of agreement (1986); Landis & Koch (1977) bands *as a declared convention*; Wilson (1927) intervals; Hackman & Oldham (1976) role clarity, Locke & Latham (1990) goal specificity, Mager & Pipe (1970) "does the person know what is expected and when"; Leventhal (1980) / Bies & Moag (1986) / Colquitt et al. (2001) procedural and interactional justice, implemented as the seal, the symmetry rule and the refusal to print a figure that could be used against a person.

**Deliberately rejected:** a 360-feedback surface (a distribution of opinions about a person); a single "alignment score" (hides the dimension-level finding that makes it actionable); storing both sides in one unsealed record (the second answer anchors on the first); auto-correcting an expectation from the divergence (that is the leader's and the report's decision); grading a future review outcome from six items (attractive, unbuildable honestly).

**Next 1–3 ambitious targets (unchanged priority, now sharper)**

- **Next 1 — [all altitudes] Authenticated identity + tenant boundary.** Server-side authorization on every read/write/export, explicit consent migration and independent review. This is the one honest limit that appears in every recent ADR, and the seal in this session makes it more visible: sealing prevents anchoring, not a determined reader with the backup file.
- **Next 2 — [manager → CEO] Temporal disclosure and repeated-release differencing.** A pair whose κ is republished every cycle is a repeated release; the confidentiality tests (complementary suppression across cycles, split/merge, inactive users, phased access) have not been written.
- **Next 3 — [frontline → director] Instrument v2 with a paired-work test.** Ask both sides to score the *same* recent piece of work against the sentence they agreed, so agreement is measured on an artifact and not only on a self-report.
## 2026-11-04 — Session 122: The Sealed Spine ([ADR-0082](docs/adr/0082-sealed-spine.md), Schema v88 no additional bump, `#/seal`, RULE-SEAL-01/02)

- **Implemented [frontline → CEO]:** a hash-chained, tamper-evident audit trail over the existing append-only event log. One `audit.seal` event per committed transaction, appended by `sealRule` registered **last** on the shared spine (62 rules), so a single seal covers every module's writes in one atomic commit. `seal = sha256(prev ‖ digest ‖ revision)` from genesis (64 zeros); verification replays the chain and reports typed failures (`chain-break`, `seal-mismatch`, `content-mismatch` at the exact revision) plus trailing-unsealed and retention-evicted blocks — evicted blocks are chain-verified and content-honestly-unverifiable, never silently clean.
- **Implemented [all altitudes]:** keyed HMAC-SHA256 when the vault is unlocked (PBKDF2 256-bit session key, domain `leados-seal-v1:`, memory-only, cleared at every lock site), plain SHA-256 otherwise — and the mode is printed on every surface, in the banner and in the identity-free integrity certificate. Seal events are exempt from the event-log retention cap (5000 vs 600) so the chain's anchors are the last thing a full log evicts.
- **Implemented [all altitudes]:** span attestation roll-up — every sealed transaction is counted at the owning span AND every leadership ancestor in the same transaction; out-of-subtree spans collapse to one aggregate row under a declared seat. `seal.scan` always runs (any rank); enable/disable/seal-pause is operator-only and fails closed under a seat via the ADR-0080 gateway (`audit-seal` right, ranks 1–5).
- **Implemented [frontline → manager]:** altitude-routed NL intake (intake `v2`): free-text drafts resolve the owning seat by lowest common ancestor over the reporting tree, suggest `ownerId` + `ownerBasis`, and the `#/intake` analysis prints an altitude-routing card (owning seat, altitude, roll-up path, routes, hand-up, forbidden). Confirming creates the case under the routed owner — so a new case's first events are sealed under the right span.
- **Zero migration:** this feature adds **no collection and no migration entry of its own** — `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays at Session 121's **88**; three settings default when absent (`sealEnabled`, `sealAutoPropagate`, `sealMode`); the chain lives in the log it protects.
- **Next 1 — [all altitudes] Authenticated identity + tenant boundary.** (Carried from Session 120.) Server-side authorization on every read/write/export; the local seat and the local seal are both workspace properties, not multi-user security.
- **Next 2 — [manager → CEO] External timestamping / signed checkpoints.** RFC 3161 or Notary-style co-signing of periodic chain checkpoints, plus write-once off-site export — the honest next step beyond a local chain (requires an external service the canonical app does not have today).
- **Next 3 — [all altitudes] Continuous background verification + reviewed adapters for legacy modules.** Re-verify on load and on a declared cadence with a visible last-verified stamp; continue extending the gateway/projection pattern module by module.
- **Rejected [all altitudes]:** claiming the chain authenticates users; claiming plain-hash mode is tamper-proof; per-person signature schemes (binding rejection: no identity bound to a seal); rebuilding the org model or adding a second one; production-RBAC claims from a browser-local seat.

## 2026-11-03 — Session 121: the note chooses the altitude (Schema v88, [ADR-0081](docs/adr/0081-altitude-router.md), `#/routing`, RULE-AR-01..03, CSV #77)

### Fresh 2026 competitive + domain hunt (fetched 2026-11-03; vendor claims are marketing, not independent benchmarks)

1. **Moveworks — intelligent triage gates on confidence.** Categorises and routes tickets by intent, urgency and historical patterns with probabilistic confidence; low-confidence/ambiguous cases go to human reviewers or clarification flows and the system **does not auto-update fields** below the threshold ([1](https://www.moveworks.com/us/en/resources/blog/what-is-intelligent-triage-it-support), 2026-03-11). *Influence:* `routingConfirm` is a single human-reviewed commit with an evidence floor and a printed refusal; a saved draft creates no case.
2. **ServiceNow Predictive Intelligence / Now Assist — classification + enrichment inside the workflow.** 2026 comparisons describe incident classification, assignment-group routing, CI/service-context enrichment, duplicate detection and SLA-risk monitoring; capability stays **platform-bound**, not universal ([2](https://www.aiuniverse.xyz/top-10-ai-ticket-triage-routing-systems-features-pros-cons-comparison/), [3](http://aiopsschool.com/blog/top-10-ai-ticket-triage-routing-systems-features-pros-cons-comparison-2/), [4](https://www.console.com/blog/best-ai-agents-for-enterprise-2026/), [5](https://www.servicenow.com/community/servicenow-otto-forum/agentic-ai-use-cases/td-p/3573516)). *Influence:* reuse the app's **own** `case.created` event so the same commit fires decisions, coaching, counterfactuals and succession — no separate integration layer.
3. **Microsoft Viva Glint / Continuous Engagement — hierarchy reporting is a confidentiality problem.** Admin-controlled pipeline, role-based access, aggregated data only, "higher of the two thresholds" enforcement, **inference prevention hides both a small group and its next higher level**, trend lines only for weeks with enough employees, and manager hierarchy breakdowns hidden when a child team is under threshold for four weeks ([6](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/viva/glint/reports/continuous-engagement-workplace-metrics), 2026-05-11). Viva Glint is **confidential, not anonymous**; ballots link to employee records; ~5 numeric / 10 verbatim thresholds; below-threshold roll-up ([7](https://invizipoll.com/blog/is-microsoft-viva-glint-anonymous), 2026-10-14). The Oct 2026 Action Taking Report adds filterable hierarchy measures and warns that activity counts are not outcomes and that small-team / reorg / inactive / phased-access scenarios must be validated ([8](https://windowsforum.com/news/viva-glint-action-taking-report-arrives-worldwide-october-2026.439920/), [9](https://tomorrowdesk.com/info/microsoft-viva-glint)). Team-level privacy-safe analytics comparisons reinforce aggregate-only, thresholded, role-scoped surfaces ([10](https://hrtechsaas.com/blog/team-level-workforce-analytics-privacy-safe-platforms/)). *Influence:* `names` / `unit` / `aggregate` disclosure ladder, small-cell refusal with a printed reason, aggregate-only brief and CSV #77, and an explicit refusal to call suppression "anonymous".

**What neither half publishes:** an out-of-sample **strictly-prior Brier skill** for its own routing, a **mean rank error** that prices the cost of sending a 7-day item to the CEO, or a **typed, auditable, idempotent** vertical roll-up written in the same transaction as the case. That is the ambition bar chased here, not a vendor feature parity claim.

### Gap analysis against the ambition bar (as found → as shipped)

- **[frontline] A note picked a module, not an altitude** → joint module × altitude report with a refusal below the evidence floor.
- **[manager] Cross-span work had no owner** → LCA of the named people's managers, printed; a `quarter` cue lifts ownership above the LCA with the reason visible.
- **[director → CEO] No vertical roll-up on intake** → `RULE-AR-01` writes one `rolls-up-to` edge to **every** leadership ancestor in the same atomic transaction as the case and its cross-module records.
- **[all altitudes] No closed loop on routing accuracy** → once-only grades, Wilson intervals, Brier skill, rank error, under/over-routing, one governed floor-breach decision per ISO week, marker-idempotent.
- **[all altitudes] Reorganisation silently invalidated a saved draft** → two-lane fingerprint over note **and** seat path; a changed tree refuses confirmation.
- **[all altitudes] Confidence gate absent** → save ≠ confirm; conflict notes never auto-adopted; peer-span confirmation refused.

### Implemented this session (tagged by altitude)

- **[frontline → CEO]** `#/routing` five panels; one parameterised read model, five disclosure forms; nav/aliases/badge/title.
- **[frontline]** Named detail, shift-level module routes, one-tap confirm with the human choosing the altitude.
- **[manager]** LCA ownership, handoff count, `names` disclosure; peer-span refusal.
- **[director]** Quarter/half-year floors, `unit` disclosure, unit-level rates and governed reliability-floor decisions.
- **[VP / executive]** Portfolio aggregates, `grades-routing` provenance, one DACI decision per breaching cell per ISO week.
- **[CEO]** Aggregate-only brief and CSV #77; no shift notes, no names, no evidence spans.
- **[all altitudes]** Additive `MIGRATIONS[87]`, fail-closed normalizers, 67/67 rule-contract parity, pausable auto-propagation with an always-available explicit scan.

### Next 1–3 ambitious targets

- **Next 1 — [all altitudes] Authenticated identity + tenant boundary.** Server-side authorization on every read/write/export, explicit consent migration, independent review. Local seat selection stays a declaration.
- **Next 2 — [frontline → CEO] Closed-loop outcome learning.** Grade *interventions*, not just routing grades, so recommendations are priced by realised outcomes rather than confidence bands.
- **Next 3 — [manager → CEO] Temporal disclosure & reorganisation differencing.** Repeated-release, split/merge, inactive-user and phased-access confidentiality tests with complementary suppression before any enterprise confidentiality claim.

### Deliberately rejected

A second NLP engine or rule spine; auto-adopting a case with no human confirmation; a generic role-themed dashboard duplicated five times; inferring altitude from sentiment, messages or keystrokes; calling suppression "anonymous" or "differentially private"; inventing a director/VP/CEO rung the roster does not contain.
## 2026-11-03 — PR #84 closed as superseded: pay-transparency candidates preserved

**Triage, not a session.** PR #84 ("Session 74 — pay architecture & equity terminal", `#/pay`, Schema v51, ADR-0039, opened 2026-10-29) was never merged. PR #85 merged the next day (2026-10-30) and took the same Schema v51 and the same ADR-0039 for the Merit & Pay-Equity Terminal (`#/merit`, `comp.js`) recorded below as Session 74. Main has since moved to Schema v87 / ADR-0080 (152 commits past #84's base); 67 of #84's 74 files conflict, including the whole test suite and the standalone artifact. It is closed as superseded, not merged. The head commit (`0d49e56`, branch `arena/9fc32624-leados`) remains reachable via `refs/pull/84/head` for reference.

**Candidates preserved from #84** — none of this exists in the shipped `#/merit` (`comp.js` has no quartile, joint-assessment or remediation machinery). A future session picking these up builds on `comp.js` under a new schema version and ADR number, not on the dead branch:

1. **Pay-quartile reporting (Directive (EU) 2023/970).** The share of each declared comparison group in each quarter of the pay distribution, per currency cohort, under the existing small-cell suppression — the Directive's reporting mechanic rather than a vendor dashboard.
2. **Joint pay assessment trigger + owned workflow.** A category gap of at least 5% unexplained by the recorded controls flags a joint pay assessment; the flag must open an owned, documented decision with attestations (e.g. "a gender-neutral job-evaluation study was completed" — recorded, never performed by the app), following the RULE-COMP-02 mechanism-not-individual pattern. The 5% figure is the Directive's; it is not a management convention.
3. **Remediation priced by re-fit, never by arithmetic.** #84's `remediationOptions` re-fits the adjusted gap model on the projected pay of each candidate correction and refuses to publish a projection when the corrected cohort cannot be re-fitted — a correction's effect is the model's, not `gap − lift`. The same discipline applies forward: re-run the gap model on a projected merit allocation to catch a matrix that quietly re-widens the gap.

**Design constraint that closed the merge path:** #84 ran its contrast on a declared closed group vocabulary (Group A / Group B); the accepted [ADR-0039](docs/adr/0039-merit-and-pay-equity-terminal.md) deliberately stores no protected characteristic and decomposes on hire origin or reporting line. The Directive's subject is sex-disaggregated pay data, so a future pay-transparency session must resolve that tension explicitly — an amended ADR with a declared, consented comparison dimension — not silently reverse the privacy stance, and not ship a second pay-equity domain beside `#/merit`.

RULE-ACL-02 writes one advisory audit marker when a cell reaches the evidence floor. Schema v85 additive migration (`MIGRATIONS[84]`), `authorityCalibrationMarkers` collection, clamped settings (`authorityCalibrationFloorN`, `authorityCalibrationReliabilityFloorPct`, `authorityCalibrationAutoPropagate`). `calibrationScan()` API action, `#/authority-calibration` route with 5 panels (Overview, By altitude, Signals, Settings, Brief), stat grid, click-through member contracts, identity-free brief download, aggregate-only CSV #74, nav/badge/aliases.

- **Rejected [all altitudes]:** a generic approval checkbox; rating/ranking individuals; inferring capacity or actual spend; autonomous spending; claiming production RBAC from a browser-local seat; auto-applying calibration remaps to contracts or settings.

- **Next 3 — [director → CEO] Authority calibration ledger.** Shipped in Session 119 (Schema v85, ADR-0079, `#/authority-calibration`). See Session 119 entry above.
- **Rejected [all altitudes]:** a generic approval checkbox; sideways peer transfers; inferring capacity or actual spend; autonomous spending; claiming production RBAC from a browser-local seat.

## 2026-11-02 — Session 117: the Succession Terminal — the bench as a certificate ([ADR-0077](docs/adr/0077-succession-terminal.md), Schema v83, `#/succession`, RULE-SUC-01..05, SUC-01..08, CSV #73)

**Implemented (ahead-of-market: every platform in the category — Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle Fusion HCM, TalentGuard, ChartHop, PeopleFluent, Darwinbox, UKG Pro — sells a *nomination plus a rated readiness colour*; none computes whether the departing holder's work can actually be reabsorbed, none prints a minimum cut when it cannot, and none prices a never-tested bench — see RESEARCH §100).** Altitudes: **F** frontline, **M** manager, **D** director, **E** exec, **C** chief.

- **[M/D/E/C]** **The unit is a span, not a seat.** One leader + their direct reports; direct reports **partition** the roster, so every obligation is tested exactly once and counts roll up by exact addition. Survivors are the holder's **peers** — the span lead never absorbs (a lead who takes their report's work has deferred the vacancy, not replaced the holder). A leader with no reports is `empty-span`, with one is `span-of-one`: both are printed as their own diagnosis, because "no bench exists" and "no evidence exists" need different fixes.
- **[M/D/E/C]** **The flow test with a printed certificate.** Real Dinic maximum flow `source → item → survivor → sink` over the span's dated obligations and the holder's peers, with the assignment read from the residual graph. When infeasible it prints the **minimum cut** — the smallest set of obligations no survivor can hold, with each item's due date and eligible-survivor count. Five graded eligibility sources (`covered-before` > `delegated-together` > `shared-goal` > `shared-review` > `same-team`), each an edge earned by a record, never a name.
- **[M/D]** **Nothing about succession is a rating.** Nominations and `readiness` rows are read as **claims** (`COVERAGE_LAYERS.claim`, weight *none*) and never enter the flow test. The subject of every verdict is a span; a person appears only as a holder with a load and a headroom, and the surface says so on the line that prints the concentration index.
- **[D/E/C]** **The enterprise number is a pair, never a point.** `∏(1 − pᵢ)` (independence reference, an upper bound) beside `maxᵢ pᵢ` (assumption-free union lower bound), with a 5% floor inside the cap and `pᵢ = 1` for a span already infeasible. Nothing is averaged that cannot be averaged; below the span floor the diffusion index refuses rather than prints a decimal.
- **[D/E/C]** **What an untested bench is worth, stated.** Lindley–Smith single-sample acceptance (`(k+1)/(k+2)`) for a span that has never run a handover — 50% at zero, above the declared floor the measured record takes over via a Jeffreys posterior. A green box is replaced by a number a chief can defend and a statement of what would falsify it.
- **[D/C]** **Money only where declared.** Per-currency daily deprivation cost typed by the leader; unpriced work is counted and never valued; no salary inferred, no band applied. Expected loss is `p × daily × days` with the exact binomial tail, and the equal-marginal shortfall is printed as an **upper bound** with its own label (Carley & Lin 1997; Artzner coherence).
- **[F↔C] Vertical roll-up on the SAME post-commit spine.** `successionRule` is registered 55th of 56, **before** `seatRule`, so a certificate edge written here must be explainable by the seat boundary above it in the same pass. `RULE-SUC-02` opens one governed DACI decision per span per 30-day bucket (three options, each with pros/cons and an explicit "accept the exposure in writing"), attaches the min-cut items with `certifies-gap` edges, `understudies-for` to the seat, `hedges-departure` to the decision — and one frontline team's gap reaches manager → director → VP → CEO in **one atomic transaction** alongside every other module's propagation (`tests/app/succession-bench.test.mjs`, cross-altitude test).
- **[all]** **Freeze, grade, refuse.** A frozen reading carries one prospective probability *and* its lower bound, the exact blocking set, verdicts, blanket and HHI; garbage in is refused (`no-measurable-span`, one-per-day). Grading is once, later, re-running the same structural test, with a deleted member **unmeasurable** and a completed obligation counted as the span *succeeding*; skill withheld below five graded readings; `Number(null)` guarded at every boundary.
- **[all]** **Zero-regression inertness.** Automatic pass gated on `successionAutoPropagate` + an operational commit; `succession.scan` and a deliberate freeze always run even with automation off. `tests/app/succession-bench.test.mjs` — 16 tests incl. max-flow cross-checked against brute-force enumeration, the overload rule in both directions, six axe-clean panels, and a committed delegation running the full 56-rule spine.
- **[all]** Wiring: Schema **v83** (`successionReadings`, `successionMarkers`, 12 declared conventions, fail-closed normalisers), `successionreading` graph node + 4 relations (97 in `LINK_RELATIONS`), 8 action commands, 13 route aliases, nav badge counting certified spans only, insights bucket, brief, **CSV #73** (`succession-bench`, aggregate-only, 30 columns, no ids/names), six panels, `docs/adr/0077-succession-terminal.md`, `INDEX.md`.

**Top next targets:**
1. **[E/C] Cryptographic seat + reading attestation** — sign each freeze with a Web Crypto key so a graded quote becomes tamper-evident; the honest prerequisite for a board-facing deployment.
2. **[M→C] Join capacity to ADR-0018.** The overload rule is a declared convention; the attention ledger measures real saturation. Feeding measured load into the headroom calculation turns the flow test from convention-driven into evidence-driven.
3. **[D/E] Evidence-based eligibility with a false-positive bound** — propose survivor edges from observed co-occurrence (shared cases, shared reviews) with an explicit error rate, instead of assuming absence of an edge means no working relationship. Print `unlinkedPairs` as the blind spot until then.
4. **[all] Seat-scoped succession export** — apply `projectForSeat` to `exportRedactedJSON` so a chief's bench pack carries counts only; then a real-browser assistive-technology walkthrough **[UNVERIFIED]**.
5. **Carried forward:** detector-level error rates, cross-terminal consistency checks, Node 20 CI diagnosis, standalone artefact's embedded source hash, detector retirement, borrowing arrival rates across lines, durable local-first outbox / multi-tab lock lease, dated FX scenario ledger, headless Chromium AT CI lane.

**Deliberately rejected:** a readiness/nine-box rebuild (the ratings exist and are the wrong object — they stay as claims); per-seat successors computed on the whole subtree (double-counts every obligation, triples the enterprise probability — the direct-report partition is load-bearing); making the span lead a survivor (defers the vacancy while printing green); predicting *who* leaves or *when* (the test assumes absence; it never forecasts a departure); reading conflicts/pulses/message text as bench inputs; inferring salary to price a vacancy; summing currencies; reporting an unmeasured span as covered; grading a probability-free reading as 0%; auto-propagating without the declared flag; a second org model beside `person.managerId`.
